hep-ex.title: Search for the low-mass isotropic signature of QCD instantons in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV using the ATLAS detector
hep-ex.author: ATLAS Collaboration
hep-ex.abstract: This Letter presents the first search for QCD instanton-induced events at the LHC. Instantons are semi-classical solutions of the Yang-Mills equations of QCD and correspond to non-perturbative tunneling between topologically distinct vacuum sectors. The search is performed in 1.6 $\text{nb}^{-1}$ of very low instantaneous luminosity proton-proton collision data collected by the ATLAS detector at 13 TeV. Angular variables based on reconstructed charged-particle tracks are used to discriminate the expected rest-frame isotropy of low-mass instanton events from the minimum-bias background. The minimum-bias event background is predicted using a data-driven technique and reweighted Monte Carlo models. A profile-likelihood fit is performed in a two-dimensional classifier variable to extract a possible signal contribution, yielding an excess of low-mass isotropic events with an observed significance of $3.5\sigma$.

hep-ex.title: AI-Assisted Analysis of CMS Open Data: Prompt J/psi Cross-Section Measurements in pp and Peripheral PbPb Collisions at sqrt(S)= 7 TeV and sqrt(sNN) = 2.76 TeV
hep-ex.author: Zhipeng Cui, Ziyu Wang, Gerry Bauer, Kai Yi
hep-ex.abstract: We investigate the use of an artificial-intelligence (AI) coding agent, supervised by human physicists, for collider physics analyses using CMS Open Data. OpenAI Codex performs dimuon event selection, two-dimensional invariant-mass and decay-length fits, Monte Carlo detector simulations, and systematic uncertainty evaluation after acquiring physics and experimental knowledge from published studies and external references, with human review at each stage. The workflow is tested on two CMS datasets, with custom full-detector simulations used to determine acceptance and reconstruction efficiencies. In proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s) = 7 TeV, prompt J/psi differential cross sections are measured versus transverse momentum and rapidity. The ratios of remeasured to published CMS cross sections have a mean of 1.000 and an RMS spread of 0.215 across 39 bins. In peripheral (50-100% centrality) PbPb collisions at sqrt(s_NN) = 2.76 TeV, the corresponding prompt J/psi fiducial cross-section ratios have a mean of 1.158 and an RMS spread of 0.225 across six intervals. We identify agent failure modes and demonstrate the importance of structured human review in ensuring reliable results.

hep-ex.title: Impact of errors-on-errors on the PDF determination from combined HERA data
hep-ex.author: Enzo Canonero, Glen Cowan, Georgia Brown, Hamed Abdolmaleki, Francesco Giuli, Alexander Glazov, Francesco Hautmann, Fredrick Olness, Pavel Starovoitov, Oleksandr Zenaiev
hep-ex.abstract: We study how the determination of parton distribution functions (PDFs) from the combined HERA inclusive deep-inelastic-scattering data is affected when the quoted sizes of the systematic errors are themselves treated as uncertain. We refer to these uncertainties informally as errors-on-errors and account for them using the Gamma Variance Model, which treats the squared quoted systematic errors as Gamma-distributed estimates of unknown variances. As a result, the usual quadratic nuisance parameter constraints in the $\chi^2$ are replaced with logarithmic ones. We present two applications of the framework. In the first, a robustness test estimates the largest errors-on-errors effects that could be present in our reproduction of the HERAPDF2.0 NNLO fit, reducing $\chi^2/n_{\rm dof}$ from 1363/1131 to 1306/1131, with the main impact concentrated at low Bjorken $x$ and low squared momentum transfer, $Q^2$. Comparable reductions are observed with a more flexible small-$x$ parametrisation, both at fixed NNLO and with NNLO+NLL$_x$ resummation. In the second, the error-on-error parameters are instead assigned a priori, as they would be in a PDF determination intended for publication. Taken together, the results indicate that errors-on-errors can account for a substantial part of the apparent data-theory tension in the combined HERA dataset, improving the inferred compatibility and widening the fitted PDF uncertainties without appreciably displacing the PDFs or cross-section predictions themselves.

Bhattacharya, M.S. Bieker, N.V. Biesuz, A. Biolchini, M. Birch, F.C.R. Bishop, A. Bitadze, A. Bizzeti, T. Blake, F. Blanc
hep-ex.abstract: An absolute calibration of the luminosity for proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV with the LHCb detector in Run 2 of the LHC is presented. The calibration cross-section of the Vertex counter, a statistic based on reconstructed primary vertices, is measured using the beam-gas imaging method to be $\sigma_\mathrm{Vertex} = 57.61 \pm 0.06\ (stat) \pm 0.52\ (syst)$ mb, corresponding to a relative precision of 0.91%. This result provides around a factor of two improvement in the precision of the LHCb luminosity calibration used in previous cross-section measurements with this dataset. The largest systematic uncertainties arise from the imperfect knowledge of the beam-gas vertex resolution, the observed fill-by-fill spread of the cross-section, and the choice of transverse beam-profile fit model.

hep-ex.title: Signatures of Leptophilic Baryogenesis at Muon Colliders
hep-ex.author: Hooman Davoudiasl, Ian M. Lewis, Miguel A. Soto Alcaraz
hep-ex.abstract: The baryon asymmetry of the Universe may be produced in a model with 3 Higgs fields, a Higgs Troika, without the need for a strong first order electroweak phase transition. The couplings of the new Higgs fields to Standard Model fermions are assumed in accord with the "Spontaneous Flavor Violation (SFV)" framework, in order to avoid large deviations from flavor physics constraints. We consider a leptophilic version of SFV and outline its potential signatures at future muon colliders, envisioned to be multi-TeV partonic center of momentum machines. Hence, they provide optimal venues to search for the leptophilic Higgs Troika baryogenesis mechanism. The projected reach for signals of the new scalars allows for probing the key components of the baryogenesis model at scales that accommodate cosmological requirements.

hep-ex.title: Feebly-Interacting Particle Searches
hep-ex.author: Jonathan L. Feng
hep-ex.abstract: In the last several years, feebly-interacting particles (FIPs) have moved from "exotica" to the mainstream of particle physics. This development is fueled by three motivations: FIPs are one of two broad possibilities for new particles, FIPs are as well motivated by dark matter as WIMPs, and FIPs are connected to important problems in particle physics. I review these motivations and then briefly highlight recent progress in a few areas, including axion-like particles, dark photons and other gauge bosons, the X17 anomaly, quirks, and the Forward Physics Facility.

hep-ex.title: Plugging the Pion Chimney
hep-ex.author: Nikita Blinov, Andrew M. Evans, Shirley Weishi Li
hep-ex.abstract: Heavy QCD axions and other gluon-coupled axion-like particles (ALPs) with masses from MeV to GeV are well motivated and have been searched for extensively. However, a window around the neutral pion mass, the so-called pion chimney, has escaped every search. There the ALP mixes strongly with the $\pi^0$ and therefore shares its experimental signatures. We show that the chimney can be closed with existing LHC data. The key point is that mixing changes the lifetimes of the two mass eigenstates but does not make them equal, and at LHC energies the states are boosted enough for the lifetime to decide whether they escape the detector or decay inside it. The ATLAS monojet search constrains the first case and the ATLAS inclusive photon measurement the second, and together they exclude the chimney up to the cutoff of the ALP effective theory. Above the cutoff, LHC searches for the colored states of the simplest ultraviolet completions exclude the rest. We also show that the bound from the $K^+$ width does not reach the chimney, because an ALP passes the same selection as a $\pi^0$, and we derive an independent, purely kinematic constraint from the measured $\pi^\pm$-$\pi^0$ mass splitting.

hep-ex.title: Probing $τ$ lepton dipole moments at multi-TeV muon colliders
hep-ex.author: Dario Buttazzo, Gabriele Levati, Yang Ma, Fabio Maltoni, Paride Paradisi, ZeQiang Wang
hep-ex.abstract: We investigate the sensitivity of future multi-TeV muon colliders to the electromagnetic and weak dipole moments of the $\tau$ lepton within the dimension-six Standard Model Effective Field Theory. We consider $\tau^+\tau^-$ production through $\mu^+\mu^-$ annihilation and vector-boson scattering, electroweak-boson-associated $\tau$ production, and the radiative Higgs decay $H\to\tau^+\tau^-\gamma$. At high energies, the dipole-induced contributions quadratic in the Wilson coefficients become particularly important, with associated Higgs production, $\mu^+\mu^-\to\tau^+\tau^-H$, providing the strongest sensitivity through energy-enhanced contact interactions. The remaining channels offer complementary probes of the underlying dipole operators. For a $10$~TeV muon collider with an integrated luminosity of $10\,\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$, we obtain combined sensitivities at the nominal $95\%$ confidence level of $|\Delta a_\tau|<1.2\times10^{-5}$, $|d_\tau|<6.6\times10^{-20}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$, $|\Delta a_\tau^Z|<1.8\times10^{-5}$, and $|d_\tau^Z|<1.0\times10^{-19}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$. Compared with FCC-ee projections, the muon collider offers substantially stronger sensitivity to the electric dipole moments, while both facilities offer complementary probes of magnetic dipole moments. These results motivate further studies incorporating realistic detector effects and systematic uncertainties.

hep-ex.title: Triangle singularity with different dynamical couplings
hep-ex.author: Jun Wang, Xiao-Hai Liu, Qiang Zhao
hep-ex.abstract: We carry out a systematic study of the impact of dynamical couplings of the vertices on the manifestations of the triangle singularity (TS) in the loop amplitude. Twelve combinations of external and internal spin-parity quantum numbers, covering the $PPS$, $VPP$, $VVP$, $VPA$, $VVV$, $VVA$, and $VVS$ effective vertices, are enumerated. Each loop amplitude is reduced via the Passarino--Veltman decomposition into scalar integrals $A_{0}$, $B_{0}$, and $C_{0}$, whose Lorentz-scalar coefficients encode the dynamical content of the vertices. Using the masses and kinematics of the $\eta(1405)\to\pi^{+}\pi^{-}\pi^{0}$ transition via the $K^{*}\bar{K}K$ loop with the intermediate $f_{0}(980)$ resonance in the $\pi^+\pi^-$ invariant spectrum as a common numerical benchmark for the twelve spin-parity assignments, we find that the same loop topology produces three distinct phenomena which manifest through the lineshapes, i.e. a narrow peak dominated by the $C_{0}$ contribution; a suppressed peak in which the $B_{0}$ and $C_{0}$ function contributions are comparable; and a cusp-like profile in which the coefficient of the leading Landau logarithm vanishes at the physical TS point. These results indicate that the visibility of a TS enhancement is not fixed by the Landau condition alone but reshaped by the detailed dynamics involved in the loop transitions.

hep-ex.title: An exact separability criterion for the $J/ψΛ$ spin state in $Λ_b^0\to J/ψ\,Λ$ decays at the LHC
hep-ex.author: Yujie Li, Xiaofan Hu, Liming Zhang
hep-ex.abstract: We derive an exact separability criterion for the spin state of the $J/\psi\Lambda$ pair produced in $\Lambda_b^0\to J/\psi(\to\mu^+\mu^-)\,\Lambda(\to p\pi^-)$ decays, taking into account the $\Lambda_b^0$ polarization at the LHC. Within the four-amplitude family $\{a_\pm,b_\pm\}$, the system is separable if and only if $(1+P_b\cos\theta)a_+b_+=(1-P_b\cos\theta)a_-b_-=P_b\sin\theta b_+b_-=0$, where $\theta$ is the $\Lambda$ production angle defined in the LHC environment. We propose a profiled likelihood ratio test to probe entanglement in the full five-dimensional angular analysis. Idealized pseudoexperiments compare this test with a negativity test and a test based on the angular moments $M_7$ and $M_9$ for rejecting the $a_+=b_-=0$ hypothesis. At both $3\sigma$ and $5\sigma$ significance, the proposed test achieves a $90\%$ rejection power with about half as many signal events as the other two methods. These results support the prospects for entanglement evidence with samples on the existing scale and for observation with larger samples.

hep-ex.title: Scalar inelastic scattering of pseudo-Majorana dark matter through a radion portal
hep-ex.author: Ruifeng Leng, Kirtimaan A. Mohan, Keping Xie, Hong-Hao Zhang
hep-ex.abstract: We investigate a radion portal for pseudo-Majorana dark matter as an interpretation of the high-recoil event LZ230616. In contrast to the familiar pseudo-Dirac regime, the pseudo-Majorana structure allows a dominant scalar transition while suppressing elastic scattering. Endothermic kinematics remove low-energy recoils, while the nuclear response shapes the surviving high-recoil spectrum. Combining the accepted LZ event count with the Born-level thermal relic abundance yields a reference solution with $m_\chi=1$ TeV, $\delta=340$ keV, and $m_r=30$ GeV. This solution lies within the published LZ spin-independent $\mathcal{O}_1^s$ interval and remains compatible with existing OPAL and CMS constraints, while a simplified HL-LHC diphoton projection could probe it. Solar neutrino searches offer a complementary test. The benchmark's energetic-daughter proxy rates are comparable in magnitude to the rate scales reconstructed from IceCube's direct $b\bar{b}$ and $\tau^+\tau^-$ templates. An illustrative IceCube-Gen2 rescaling suggests future sensitivity, while a model-specific assessment requires the radion-cascade neutrino spectra and detector response.

hep-ex.title: Universal Mass Equation for Equal-Quantum Excited-States Sets~III
hep-ex.author: L. David Roper(VTech), Igor Strakovsky(GWU)
hep-ex.abstract: Using our simple logarithmic Universal Mass Equation, we considered heavy non-$q\bar{q}$ meson states. PDG2026 reported a series of mesons with quantum numbers not allowed for standard $q\bar{q}$ states. Using LQCD predictions, we evaluated a scalar $0^{++}$ and tensor $2^{++}$ glueball series for which predictions are available. This approach allows us to predict heavy states that require future experimental studies. Additionally, we consider the possible misidentification of some meson states.

hep-ex.title: Muon Collider: Towards the Energy Frontier
hep-ex.author: Mark A. Palmer, Daniel Schulte, Vladimir Shiltsev
hep-ex.abstract: A muon collider has emerged as a compelling candidate for the next energy-frontier particle accelerator, combining the discovery potential of multi-TeV lepton collisions with a footprint and power consumption far smaller than existing or proposed hadron and electron-positron colliders. Advances over the past two decades in high-power targets, muon production and capture, ionization cooling, rapid acceleration, high-field magnets, collider ring design, and machine-detector integration have transformed the concept from a long-term vision into a credible path toward a future flagship facility. This review summarizes the physics opportunities, the accelerator complex's design and status, the unique experimental environment, recent technical achievements, ongoing international R&D, and remaining steps toward realizing a high-energy muon collider by the middle of the century.

hep-ex.title: Loop-induced $gg\to ZH$ at NLO+PS for LHC simulations: exact, fast scale and PDF event weights, theory uncertainties, and the limits of rescaled LO+PS
hep-ex.author: Licheng Zhang, Christopher Palmer
hep-ex.abstract: We study loop-induced $gg\to ZH$ production with charged-lepton and neutrino $Z$ decays at next-to-leading order (NLO) in QCD matched to parton showers, using public software at $\sqrt{s}=13$ and 13.6 TeV. An exact loop-amplitude cache reduces event-generation time by a factor of 26 with 450 scale and PDF weights, while Born suppression improves boosted-event statistics without changing the weighted prediction. We present inclusive results for both channels and charged-lepton differential and STXS Stage 1.3 predictions with theory uncertainties. At 13.6 TeV, fixed-order top-quark mass-scheme variations transferred to NLO+PS dominate the statistically precise central-Higgs STXS bins for $p_\mathrm{T}^V\ge150$ GeV, reaching 32-50%. An inclusive $K$ factor does not reproduce the boosted and jet-dependent NLO+PS spectra of the tested LO+PS samples, and the differences depend strongly on the shower prescription. For specified CMS- and ATLAS-style vetoed sources at 13.6 TeV, we construct separate charged-lepton and neutrino corrections using ensembles of gradient-boosted classifiers, with calibration, target-theory variations and transfer uncertainties. Independent tests show substantial improvement over inclusive rescaling in most tested distributions, but not uniform closure. In charged-lepton calibration comparisons, the median STXS uncertainty from transported NLO scales and transfer terms is 17% for both the CMS- and ATLAS-style corrections, compared with LO scale uncertainties of 28% and 26% at fixed $K$. These comparisons do not include the complete target-theory budget. The corrections do not restore the depleted hard-recoil population; the highest ATLAS-style $p_\mathrm{T}^H$ bin stays below NLO+PS even at the upper edge of its band. The setup, reference results, and source- and channel-specific models support new NLO+PS generation and reuse of existing samples within stated limits.

hep-ex.title: Precision Muon Physics
hep-ex.author: Tim Gorringe
hep-ex.abstract: The muon has become a versatile tool for fundamental physics. Measurements of muon decay determine the Fermi constant and establish the chiral structure of weak interactions. Measurements with stored muons and bound muons enable precision determinations of the muon charge, mass, and magnetic moment. These studies also provide far-reaching tests of bound-state QED and the Standard Model, as well as unique sensitivity to physics beyond our current understanding of the particles, forces, and laws of nature. We survey the landscape of precision muon physics, emphasizing both the physics reach and the experimental breadth. We highlight the range of techniques, from charged-particle timing, tracking, and polarimetry to storage-ring experiments, microwave resonance methods, and Doppler-free laser spectroscopy. We also describe the interplay between experimental work and theoretical developments in quantum electrodynamics, quantum chromodynamics, and effective field theory.

hep-ex.title: Precision Measurements of the Electroweak Mixing Angle in the Region of the Z pole at the Large Hadron Collider
hep-ex.author: Arie Bodek, Hyon-San Seo, Un-Ki Yang
hep-ex.abstract: In the Standard Model (SM), the effective leptonic weak mixing angle $\sin^2\theta^\ell_{\rm eff}$ can be predicted to very high accuracy by using the experimental values of the mass of the Z boson ($M_Z$), the Fermi constant, the fine structure constant, the mass of Higgs boson, the quark masses, and the value of the Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) strong coupling ($\alpha_s$) at $M_Z$. Therefore, deviations of measurements from SM predictions can be indications of new physics. With recent advances in experimental and analysis techniques, measurements of $\sin^2\theta^\ell_{\rm eff}$ at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), extracted from the forward-backward asymmetry ($A_{\rm FB}$) in Drell-Yan dilepton events, are now competitive with previously published measurements at $e^+e^-$ collider experiments. We report on a more precise extraction of the effective leptonic weak mixing angle via an updated analysis of the CMS Drell-Yan $A_{\rm FB}$ measurements at 13 TeV. We obtain $\sin^2\theta^\ell_{\rm eff}$=0.23154$\pm$0.00024 with additional PDF constraints from measurements of the W decay lepton charge asymmetry at 13 TeV and the W/Z cross section ratios. It is the most precise single experiment measurement to date and is in excellent agreement with the SM 2026 indirect prediction of 0.23152$\pm$0.00006.

hep-ex.title: Prospect for measurement of CP-violating parameters of $B_s^0 \to ϕγ$ at the Tera Z factory
hep-ex.author: Hengyu Wang, Hanhua Cui, Yongfeng Zhu, Hao Liang, Yuexin Wang, Kaili Zhang, Yi Wang, Weizheng Song, Lingfeng Li, Shanzhen Chen, Manqi Ruan
hep-ex.abstract: $b \to s\gamma$ transition is a critical flavor-changing neutral current (FCNC) process that could be used to probe CP violation (CPV) and new physics (NP). We quantify the anticipated precision for measuring $B_s^0 \to \phi\gamma$ at the CEPC Z pole operation, showing that the relative statistical uncertainty could be as low as 0.16\%, improved by approximately two orders of magnitude compared to existing measurements. Additionally, we perform a time-dependent analysis of the $B_s^0 \to \phi\gamma$ decay, accounting for $B_s^0/\bar{B}_s^0$ mixing extract the mixing-induced and CP-violating parameters $\boldsymbol{\mathcal{A}_{\phi\gamma}^\Delta}$, $\boldsymbol{C_{\phi\gamma}}$ and $\boldsymbol{S_{\phi\gamma}}$. Using central value from LHCb measurement as input, we evaluate the anticipated accuracy of measurements of these parameters. The projected statistical uncertainties are $\sigma_{A_{\phi\gamma}^{\Delta}{}^{\text{stat}}} = 0.021$, $\sigma_C^{\text{stat}} = 0.0092$ and $\sigma_S^{\text{stat}} = 0.0096$, and the systematic uncertainties are $\sigma_{A_{\phi\gamma}^{\Delta}{}^{\text{syst}}} = 0.035$, $\sigma_C^{\text{syst}} = 0.0027$ and $\sigma_S^{\text{syst}} = 0.0064$. Furthermore, the 1$\sigma$ sensitivity boundaries for NP in this study are found to be $\mathcal{A}_{\phi\gamma}^\Delta < -0.05$ or $\mathcal{A}_{\phi\gamma}^\Delta > 0.15$, $\mathcal{C}_{\phi\gamma} < -0.02$ or $\mathcal{C}_{\phi\gamma} > 0.04$, and $\mathcal{S}_{\phi\gamma} < -0.04$ or $\mathcal{S}_{\phi\gamma} > 0.04$. We also conduct a relevant detector optimization study by establishing the correlation between the anticipated precision and the intrinsic resolution of the ECAL, as well as the performance of the PID system.

hep-ex.title: A machine-learning method for the estimation of the background from jets misidentified as hadronic tau lepton decays
hep-ex.author: CMS Collaboration
hep-ex.abstract: Backgrounds arising from quark- and gluon-initiated jets misidentified as hadronically decaying tau leptons constitute a major experimental challenge for analyses involving tau leptons. The MUltivariate Fake-Factor INference (MUFFIN) approach, a machine-learning-based method for estimating this background directly from observed events, is presented. Boosted decision tree reweighting is used to learn multidimensional, per-object correction factors directly from observed data, thereby modelling the jet to hadronic tau lepton misidentification probability across the kinematic and topological phase space without relying on low-dimensional parametrisations. Performance studies are presented using proton-proton collision data collected by the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13.6 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 62.4 fb$^{-1}$. Compared to low-dimensional parametrisation methods, improved modelling of key kinematic observables is achieved, particularly in regions of high $p_\mathrm{T}$. The improved modelling leads to a reduction of up to 70% in the systematic uncertainty associated with jets being misidentified as hadronically decaying tau leptons. The MUFFIN method provides a robust and scalable method for background estimation in precision measurements and searches for beyond-the-standard-model physics involving tau lepton final states.

hep-ex.title: LH$μ$C Concept: Energy-Frontier Antimuon-Proton Collisions at CERN
hep-ex.author: Arda Goroglu, Saleh Sultansoy
hep-ex.abstract: The concept of the LH$\mu$C, an energy-frontier antimuon-proton collider based on the HL-LHC, is presented. After recalling why energy-frontier lepton-hadron colliders are indispensable as QCD explorers and reviewing the history of muon-proton collider proposals, two ways of realising $\mu p$ collisions at the LHC are compared: with muon-collider beams and with ultra-cold $\mu^+$ beams as proposed for $\mu$TRISTAN. For the latter, a $\mu$TRISTAN-type booster and the re-use of the LHeC energy-recovery-linac tunnel are discussed; colliding 1 TeV antimuons with 7 TeV protons gives $\sqrt{s}=5.3$ TeV and peak luminosities of $8.8\times10^{33}$ and $7.2\times10^{33}$ cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$, respectively. The detector concept and the physics potential, including searches for colour-octet muons and R-parity-violating squarks, are discussed together with the main challenges.

hep-ex.title: Global Fit of Modified Quark Couplings to EW Gauge Bosons and Vector-Like Quarks in Light of the Cabibbo Angle Anomaly
hep-ex.author: Andreas Crivellin, Matthew Kirk, Teppei Kitahara, Federico Mescia
hep-ex.abstract: There are two tensions related to the Cabibbo angle of the CKM matrix. First, the determinations of $V_{us}$ from $K_{\mu 2}$, $K_{\ell3}$, and $\tau$ decays disagree at the $3\sigma$ level. Second, using the average of these results in combination with $\beta$ decays (including super-allowed $\beta$ decays and neutron decay), a deficit in first-row CKM unitarity with a significance of again about $3\sigma$ is found. These discrepancies, known as the Cabibbo Angle anomaly, can in principle be solved by modifications of $W$ boson couplings to quarks. However, due to $SU(2)_L$ invariance, $Z$ couplings to quarks are also modified and flavour changing neutral currents can occur. In order to consistently assess the agreement of a new physics hypothesis with data, we perform a combined analysis for all dimension-six Standard Model Effective Field Theory operators that generate modified $W$ couplings to first and second generation quarks. We then study models with vector-like quarks, which are prime candidates for a corresponding UV completion as they can affect $W$-quark couplings at tree level, and we perform a global fit including flavour observables (in particular loop effects in $\Delta F=2$ processes). We find that the best fit can be obtained for the $SU(2)_L$ doublet vector-like quark $Q$ as it can generate right-handed $W$-$u$-$d$ and $W$-$u$-$s$ couplings as preferred by data.

hep-ex.title: Transverse Energy--Energy Correlators at Small $x$ for Photon--Hadron Production
hep-ex.author: Zhong-Bo Kang, Robert Kao, Meijian Li, Jani Penttala
hep-ex.abstract: We study the transverse energy--energy correlator (TEEC) observable in photon--hadron and photon--jet production in p+p and p+A collisions at small $x$. We derive the relevant expressions in the high-energy limit of the scattering where the dipole picture is applicable and show how the dependence on the fragmentation function of the hadron cancels due to the momentum-sum rule. The nonperturbative scattering with the target nucleus is expressed in terms of the dipole amplitude, which also describes nonlinear gluon saturation effects. The TEEC observable is computed in the RHIC and LHC kinematics, and we show that it can be sensitive to the dipole amplitude, making it a potentially good observable for studying saturation effects.

hep-ex.title: Keeping It Renormalizable: Minimal Baryogenesis induced Asymmetric Dark Matter
hep-ex.author: Miguel Escudero, Thomas Hambye, Chandan Hati
hep-ex.abstract: Many asymmetric dark matter scenarios have been proposed to date. Among them, perhaps the most motivated ones are those in which the dark matter asymmetry is induced from the baryon/lepton asymmetries via chemical equilibration without any new sources of CP violation. However, most of the models put forward along these lines have been excluded by now and/or are based on complicated setups. In this letter, we present a new, simple, and viable scenario. It assumes only two new fields: a scalar singlet and an inert scalar doublet, and is based only on renormalizable interactions, that slowly generate the dark matter asymmetry from the Standard Model Higgs asymmetry. The successful asymmetry transfer requires small (but technically natural) couplings which in turn make the model CP conserving in practice. The model allows for the direct detection of dark matter in the upcoming generation of experiments, and the inert doublet is predicted to be light enough to be potentially produced and observed at the LHC and future colliders, $46\,{\rm GeV}<m_{H'}<580\,{\rm GeV}$. Quite remarkably, the mass and lifetime of the inert doublet may be inferred from direct detection experiments, indicating long-lived compressed electroweak states that can be searched for at the HL-LHC.

hep-ex.title: SURFing to the Fundamental Limit of Jet Tagging
hep-ex.author: Ian Pang, Darius A. Faroughy, David Shih, Ranit Das, Gregor Kasieczka
hep-ex.abstract: Beyond the practical goal of improving search and measurement sensitivity through better jet tagging algorithms, there is a deeper question: what are their upper performance limits? Generative surrogate models with learned likelihood functions offer a new approach to this problem, provided the surrogate correctly captures the underlying data distribution. In this work, we introduce the SUrrogate ReFerence (SURF) method, a new approach to validating generative models. This framework enables exact Neyman-Pearson tests by training the target model on samples from another tractable surrogate, which is itself trained on real data. We argue that the EPiC-FM generative model is a valid surrogate reference for JetClass jets and apply SURF to show that modern jet taggers may already be operating close to the true statistical limit. By contrast, we find that autoregressive GPT models unphysically exaggerate top vs. QCD separation power encoded in the surrogate reference, implying that they are giving a misleading picture of the fundamental limit.

hep-ex.title: Inclusive and multiplicity-dependent pseudorapidity densities of charged particles in pp collisions at $\mathbf{\sqrt{s} = 13.6}$ TeV
hep-ex.author: ALICE Collaboration
hep-ex.abstract: The distribution of the pseudorapidity density of primary charged particles (${\rm d}N_{\rm ch}/ {\rm d}\eta$) in $|\eta|<1.5$ is measured in pp collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 13.6 TeV using the ALICE detector. Tracks are reconstructed with the upgraded Inner Tracking System and Time Projection Chamber, and results are reported for events having at least one charged particle in $|\eta|<1$. The multiplicity dependence of the pseudorapidity density of charged particles is also explored with the multiplicity determined by the forward detectors.The average charged-particle pseudorapidity density at midrapidity ($|\eta|<0.5$) is measured to be $\langle \mathrm{d}N_{\mathrm{ch}}/\mathrm{d}\eta \rangle = 7.10 \pm 0.20$. Combined with lower-energy measurements, the results follow a power-law scaling with the center-of-mass energy. These measurements provide a new reference for charged-particle production at the highest proton$-$proton collision energy available at the LHC.

hep-ex.title: Dispersive analysis of the $\boldsymbol{ϕ\to γπ^0 π^0}$ process
hep-ex.author: Bai-Long Hoid, Igor Danilkin, Marc Vanderhaeghen
hep-ex.abstract: We present an analysis of the radiative decay $\phi \to \gamma \pi^0 \pi^0$ in a dispersive framework, where the two-pion subsystem undergoes strong final-state interactions that cover the $f_0(500)$ and $f_0(980)$ regions. We employ a coupled-channel Muskhelishvili-Omnès framework that allows for a consistent treatment of two scalar resonances and crossed-channel singularities induced by the Born and vector-meson exchanges. We explicitly verify the equivalence between the modified and standard Muskhelishvili-Omnès representations for vector-meson pole contributions when the isoscalar Omnès matrix is chosen asymptotically bounded, and we adopt the standard representation in decay kinematics. This yields, for the first time, a parameter-free dispersive prediction for the kaon Born rescattering, which provides a dominant contribution. To obtain a good fit to the KLOE and SND data, we employ a once-subtracted coupled-channel dispersion relation with heavier left-hand cut contributions and two unknown subtraction constants. The results demonstrate the consistency among the data for $\pi\pi$ scattering, $\gamma\gamma$ fusion, and $\phi $ radiative decay, thereby validating the underlying dispersive formalism and the input used for the hadronic Omnès matrix and left-hand cuts.

hep-ex.title: One-point energy correlator for deep inelastic scattering at small $x$
hep-ex.author: Zhong-Bo Kang, Robert Kao, Meijian Li, Jani Penttala
hep-ex.abstract: We derive the expressions for the one-point energy correlator (OPEC) in deep inelastic scattering in the high-energy (small-$x$) limit within the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) framework. The OPEC is computed as a function of the angle between the energy flow and the target proton or nucleus, enabling a systematic exploration of different momentum scales in the scattering process. Owing to the momentum sum rule, the dependence on fragmentation functions cancels, leaving the dipole amplitude as the only nonperturbative input. As a result, the OPEC provides a sensitive and promising probe of gluon saturation dynamics at small $x$. We present numerical results for representative kinematic configurations relevant to the future Electron--Ion Collider, demonstrating sizable nuclear suppression effects within the CGC framework and highlighting the consistency of this observable with predictions from gluon saturation.

hep-ex.title: Improved Pion-Kaon Identification in Heavy-Ion Collisions with a Two-Dimensional Transformation
hep-ex.author: Shaowei Lan, Bijun Fan, Like Liu
hep-ex.abstract: Accurate identification of charged pions and kaons is essential for precision measurements in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, but becomes increasingly challenging at intermediate and high transverse momentum because of the increasing overlap of the TPC and TOF particle identification responses. In this work, we quantitatively benchmark a two-dimensional shift-and-rotation PID procedure that combines the $n\sigma_{\pi}$ and mass-squared $(m^{2})$ information. The benchmark is performed using Au+Au collision events generated with the AMPT model, where the detector response is modeled using $p_{T}$-dependent PID parameters extracted from STAR data. Since the true particle identities and input yields are known in AMPT but are not used during the reconstruction, the procedure can be evaluated through a direct closure test that is not possible with experimental data alone. The two-dimensional procedure is compared with a reference one-dimensional method consisting of an $|n\sigma_{\pi}|<$ 3 preselection followed by a Gaussian fit to the $m^{2}$ distribution. While both methods perform well when pion and kaon PID responses are well separated, the two-dimensional procedure provides improved yield closure as the PID distributions increasingly overlap at high $p_{T}$. The reconstructed-to-input yield ratio remains within 2\% of unity up to $p_T =$ 3 GeV/$c$, whereas the reference one-dimensional procedure shows a larger deviation. Reaction-plane $v_{2}$ closure tests show that both the reference one-dimensional and two-dimensional PID procedures reproduce the AMPT input $v_{2}$ within the statistical uncertainties over the studied $p_{T}$ range. These results demonstrate that the two-dimensional procedure substantially improves the high-$p_{T}$ yield reconstruction without introducing a detectable bias in the extracted $v_{2}$ under the STAR-like detector response considered here.

Farrag, A. R. Fazely, A. Fedynitch, N. Feigl, C. Finley, D. Fox, A. Franckowiak, S. Fukami, P. Fürst
hep-ex.abstract: We present IceCube's latest release of muon track data for neutrino point-source searches, extending the previously published 10-year dataset to cover 14 years of observations (April 6, 2008 - May 23, 2022). This release features an updated event selection and improved detector calibration for data recorded after June 1, 2010. The release also includes binned instrument response functions and effective areas, enabling the community to perform sensitive searches for steady and transient neutrino sources. We report on key science results obtained with this dataset using internal IceCube analysis tools and compare them to those derived from analyses based on the binned response functions included in this public release. To facilitate reproducible research, we provide benchmark results obtained using this data release and publicly available software. This release represents IceCube's most sensitive and comprehensive publicly available all-sky muon track dataset to date and should be preferred over previous releases.

hep-ex.title: Dispersive analysis of the $\boldsymbol{J/ψ\to γπ^0 π^0}$ process
hep-ex.author: Bai-Long Hoid, Igor Danilkin, Anna Testa, Marc Vanderhaeghen
hep-ex.abstract: We present a dispersive amplitude analysis of the low-energy $\pi^0\pi^0$ system in the radiative decay $J/\psi\to\gamma\pi^0\pi^0$, using the mass-independent BESIII $0^{++}$ and $2^{++}$ intensities, the total spectrum, and the measured $0^{++}-2^{++}$ $E1$ phase difference. The isoscalar $S$-wave is described by a coupled-channel $\pi\pi/K\bar K$ Muskhelishvili-Omnès representation, which implements the strong final-state interactions associated with the $f_0(500)$ and $f_0(980)$. The $D$-wave is treated with a single-channel $\pi\pi$ Muskhelishvili-Omnès representation, where we identify all kinematic constraints of helicity amplitudes before transforming them to the experimental $E1$, $M2$, and $E3$ multipoles. Smooth short-distance production of a pseudoscalar-meson pair is encoded in subtraction polynomials, while left-hand-cut effects are estimated and found to be numerically subleading. We identify the negative solution of the BESIII $0^{++}-2^{++}$ $E1$ phase ambiguity, after using the modulo-$\pi$ freedom of production amplitudes, as the phase solution compatible with unitarity constraints, showing that the measured phase information can be accommodated with the Omnès phase motion without requiring large additional phases. By normalizing the BESIII intensities with the extracted branching fraction, we fix the absolute scale of the fitted amplitudes, making them suitable as input for future dispersive studies of two-pion contributions to gravitational form factors.

hep-ex.title: The muon Moonshot: Moon subsurface tomography with upward-going muons
hep-ex.author: Zimo Hu, Leyun Gao, Zhengyun You, Qite Li, Qiang Li, Yuhong Yu, Liangwen Chen, Xueheng Zhang, Zhiyu Sun
hep-ex.abstract: We propose a novel muon Moonshot concept for lunar subsurface tomography based on upward-going muons originating from the lunar regolith. Unlike Earth, the Moon lacks an atmosphere, leaving dense regolith below and a near-vacuum environment above. Consequently, most downward-going hadrons are absorbed before decaying, while upward-going hadrons escaping the regolith can decay in flight, producing a significant flux of lunar muons. These muons can be detected by instruments on the lunar surface or in near-lunar orbit. We perform Monte Carlo simulations to investigate their energy spectra, angular distributions, and integrated fluxes under various theoretical and detector configurations. The results indicate that the lunar muon flux is sensitive to detector altitude under idealized geometry. This dependence demonstrates its potential as a novel, non-invasive probe of shallow subsurface voids. We also present case studies on the detection of underground cavities and water resources. For shallow overburden, large cavity signals remain detectable with estimated backgrounds and systematics. Weaker water signals remain challenging. Potential implementations in future lunar missions are also discussed.

hep-ex.title: Polarized observables in $τ\to VV ν_τ$ decays
hep-ex.author: Vindhyawasini Prasad, Hiroyuki Umeeda
hep-ex.abstract:
We study polarization observables in $	au^- 	o V_1^- V_2^0 
u_	au$ decays for $(V_1^-, V_2^0)=(ho^-, ho^0), (ho^-, \omega), (K^{*-}, ho^0), (K^{*-}, \omega), (ho^-,  ar{K}^{*0})$ using the helicity formalism. While the obtained branching fraction for $	au^-	o ho^-ho^0
u_	au$ is consistent with that of angular momentum algebra method, the results for the other four channels are comparable with (smaller than) those from the effective chiral model (the aforementioned method). Our results for the longitudinal polarization fractions $f_L$ indicate that nonnegligible corrections to the endpoint limit ($f_L = 1/3$), a consequence of Lorentz symmetry, are present at the scale of tau mass. Future measurements of $f_L$ at Belle II for $	au^- 	o V_1^- V_2^0 
u_	au$ decays will provide crucial information on polarization patterns observed in nonleptonic charm decays.

hep-ex.title: Amplified Isospin Breaking from Coupled-Channel Dynamics Near Threshold
hep-ex.author: Xiang-Kun Dong, Feng-Kun Guo, Christoph Hanhart, Teng Ji, Ulf-G. Meißner
hep-ex.abstract: We identify the dynamical origin of amplified isospin breaking in near-threshold states. Using a pole-residue-based measure defined directly from the pole couplings, rather than from decay observables that are also affected by different final-state kinematics, we show that threshold proximity of the pole alone is insufficient: large isospin breaking requires a sizable interaction in the companion isospin channel. In particular, the isospin-violating pole-coupling ratio vanishes when the companion-channel interaction is switched off, even at finite threshold splitting. Applied to the $X(3872)$, the observed large isospin breaking points to a nearby partner pole, $W_{c1}$, as predicted in previous studies. As a concrete realization of the previously discussed leading/shadow-pole interchange, we find that the $W_{c1}$ pole, which predominantly affects the line shapes near the charged threshold in the physical case, does not evolve into the pure $I=1$ eigenstate in the isospin limit; instead, that eigenstate is continuously connected to a more distant shadow pole.

hep-ex.title: Optimisation of importance sampling implementation in rare-event shielding simulations using Geant4
hep-ex.author: P. Knights, L. J. Milligan, K. Nikolopoulos
hep-ex.abstract: Rare-event search experiments demand ever-lower backgrounds, and the resulting radio-pure materials and suppressive shielding make related background simulations computationally expensive without event biasing. We present a method for optimising the widely used importance splitting and Russian roulette technique for rare-event searches, in which a whole number of equal-width importance layers fill the shielding geometry. Balancing relative uncertainty against execution time, we optimise the layer thickness for both $\gamma$-rays and neutrons, and across different shielding materials and thicknesses. Expressed as a multiple of the primary particle's mean free path, the optimal thickness generalises across energies for a given particle type and yields a physics-based prediction applicable to any shielding design. The same trend reveals that over-biasing is possible, with relative uncertainty worsening at high layer counts for fixed execution time. The optimal configuration gives an $\mathcal{O}$(20) gain in computational efficiency over the unbiased case.

hep-ex.title: Reassessing the $X(2370)$ in $J/ψ\toγK_S^0K_S^0π^0$ beyond the one-dimensional mass projections
hep-ex.author: Xiang-Kun Dong, Teng Ji, Meike Küßner, Ulf-G. Meißner
hep-ex.abstract: The BESIII Collaboration recently extracted the properties of the $X(2370)$ from a fit to the one-dimensional $K_S^0K_S^0\pi^0$ invariant-mass spectrum in $J/\psi\to\gamma K_S^0K_S^0\pi^0$. The intermediate two-body structures visible in the mass correlations, including the $K_0^*(1430)$ bands, require a coherent treatment of cross-channel interference when interpreting the enhancement near 2.3 GeV. We reassess the need for an additional $X(2370)$ contribution by fitting the published data using an effective coupled-channel framework with an approximate detection efficiency depending on the three-body invariant mass. The three-body parent amplitude is parameterized using a $K$-matrix that describes scattering among several quasi-two-body channels. The seven- and eight-bare-state models give similar mass distributions. Adding the eighth bare state lowers the Poisson deviance by 1.22% and produces an additional pole at $E=(2419-i152)$ MeV, substantially broader than the $X(2370)$ mass-width reference. This pole is model-dependent, and its identification with the $X(2370)$ is not clear. The present analysis does not establish the need for an additional $X(2370)$ contribution in $J/\psi\to\gamma K_S^0K_S^0\pi^0$, thereby weakening the flavor-singlet argument based on the suppression of $K^*\bar K$ relative to the total $K\bar K\pi$ contribution. A more comprehensive experimental amplitude analysis, incorporating coherent interference, mass and angular correlations, and detector effects across related decay channels, is needed to establish the role and decay properties of the $X(2370)$.

hep-ex.title: Proton generalized parton distributions from electromagnetic form factors: A theoretically constrained phenomenological reconstruction
hep-ex.author: A. Capelo-Astudillo, T. Aguilar, M. Conde-Correa, A. Duenas-Vidal, P. G. Ortega, J. Segovia
hep-ex.abstract: We present a theoretically constrained phenomenological reconstruction of the unpolarized, chiral-even, leading-twist proton generalized parton distributions $H^q$ and $E^q$. At zero skewness, valence-quark distributions are combined with flavor-dependent exponential profiles calibrated simultaneously against phenomenological representations of the proton and neutron electromagnetic form factors. The construction imposes exact valence and anomalous-magnetic-moment normalizations, the low-scale condition $B^{u+d}(0)=0$, the required endpoint behavior, and the complete Gaussian impact-parameter positivity bound. The resulting parametrization provides a reasonable description of the electromagnetic form factors and their slopes while revealing the tension between strict GPD consistency and a precision reproduction of all low-$Q^2$ observables within the adopted ansatz. We extend the distributions to nonzero skewness using normalized double distributions and introduce an independent $D$-term to complete the relevant Mellin polynomials. We examine electromagnetic and energy--momentum-tensor form factors, impact-parameter distributions, positivity, polynomiality, and illustrative mechanical properties. The analysis distinguishes information constrained by electromagnetic data from additional assumptions governing skewness and the mechanical sector, thereby providing a transparent elastic baseline for future studies of nucleon-to-resonance transition GPDs.

hep-ex.abstract: We investigate the sensitivity of the ESSnuSB large underground water-Cherenkov (WC) detector to two key solar neutrino signatures: the MSW spectral upturn in the $^8$B electron neutrino survival probability $P_{ee}(E_\nu)$, and the first direct observation of the rare hep neutrino flux. The analysis incorporates detector systematic uncertainties (energy resolution and flux normalization) and models environmental backgrounds from cosmic-ray muon spallation and $^{222}$Rn contamination. We adopt a shape-driven analysis strategy with a floating overall normalization, so that the discovery power relies on the spectral distortion rather than on the absolute event rate. In a realistic scenario with 90% spallation rejection efficiency, informed by the Super-Kamiokande experience and recent JUNO analyses, residual spallation backgrounds prevent either signal from reaching $5\sigma$ significance within 20 years of exposure. For the hep flux, we present a detailed sensitivity study to both its discovery and its precision, and quantify how the required spallation veto efficiency and recoil energy threshold jointly determine the achievable significance for both signals. At the adopted thresholds, discovery-level sensitivity for both signals requires approximately 99% spallation rejection over a 20-year exposure.

hep-ph.title: 21 cm Cosmology of Boosted Dark Matter
hep-ph.author: Min Sub Lee, Jeong Han Kim, Kyoungchul Kong, Jong-Chul Park
hep-ph.abstract: The formation history of low-mass halos is sensitive to the properties of dark matter. At low redshift, nonlinear evolution and baryonic processes can obscure this information. The 21 cm signal provides access to a high-redshift stage of structure formation, when the abundance and clustering of low-mass halos retain direct sensitivity to the mass and interactions of dark matter. Boosted dark matter (BDM) realizes this possibility through a two-component scenario in which the annihilation of the heavier component converts part of the mass difference into kinetic energy of the lighter component. Self-interactions redistribute this energy and generate pressure support, suppressing small-scale density perturbations even for dark matter masses in the MeV range. We calculate the global 21 cm brightness temperature and its power spectrum in BDM cosmology. The reduced abundance of low-mass halos delays the global absorption feature and shifts the characteristic redshift evolution of the power spectrum. We assess the projected sensitivity of SKA1-Low to these signatures. The sensitivity is strongest at intermediate light-component fractions, where both components remain sufficiently abundant for self-heating to affect structure formation. For $\sigma_{\rm self1}/m_1\simeq0.1\,{\rm cm^2\,g^{-1}}$, models with $0.2\lesssim r_1\lesssim0.7$ can be distinguished from the fiducial $\Lambda$CDM prediction at the $95\%$ confidence level under the optimistic forecast. We compare our results with existing direct-detection bounds from SENSEI and prospects for BDM searches at large-volume neutrino experiments, including Super-/Hyper-Kamiokande, JUNO, and DUNE. This comparison highlights the unique and complementary role of high-redshift surveys in testing BDM models.

hep-ph.title: Feebly-Interacting Particle Searches
hep-ph.author: Jonathan L. Feng
hep-ph.abstract: In the last several years, feebly-interacting particles (FIPs) have moved from "exotica" to the mainstream of particle physics. This development is fueled by three motivations: FIPs are one of two broad possibilities for new particles, FIPs are as well motivated by dark matter as WIMPs, and FIPs are connected to important problems in particle physics. I review these motivations and then briefly highlight recent progress in a few areas, including axion-like particles, dark photons and other gauge bosons, the X17 anomaly, quirks, and the Forward Physics Facility.

hep-ph.title: Plugging the Pion Chimney
hep-ph.author: Nikita Blinov, Andrew M. Evans, Shirley Weishi Li
hep-ph.abstract: Heavy QCD axions and other gluon-coupled axion-like particles (ALPs) with masses from MeV to GeV are well motivated and have been searched for extensively. However, a window around the neutral pion mass, the so-called pion chimney, has escaped every search. There the ALP mixes strongly with the $\pi^0$ and therefore shares its experimental signatures. We show that the chimney can be closed with existing LHC data. The key point is that mixing changes the lifetimes of the two mass eigenstates but does not make them equal, and at LHC energies the states are boosted enough for the lifetime to decide whether they escape the detector or decay inside it. The ATLAS monojet search constrains the first case and the ATLAS inclusive photon measurement the second, and together they exclude the chimney up to the cutoff of the ALP effective theory. Above the cutoff, LHC searches for the colored states of the simplest ultraviolet completions exclude the rest. We also show that the bound from the $K^+$ width does not reach the chimney, because an ALP passes the same selection as a $\pi^0$, and we derive an independent, purely kinematic constraint from the measured $\pi^\pm$-$\pi^0$ mass splitting.

hep-ph.title: Supernova Bounds on Neutrino Dipole Moments from a Modern Perspective
hep-ph.author: Damiano F. G. Fiorillo, Martina La Rosa, Federico Testagrossa, Edoardo Vitagliano
hep-ph.abstract: Neutrinos may have nonstandard magnetic dipole moments $\mu_\nu$. In the dense cores of supernovae (SNe), these would convert part of the neutrinos into sterile, right-handed states through the electromagnetic fluctuations of the charged plasma. The streaming sterile neutrinos with 100-MeV energies can convert back to standard neutrinos in the Galactic magnetic field, leading to a high-energy neutrino flux unobserved from the historical SN 1987A. We reassess the production rates, including scattering on both protons and electrons, and, building upon advances in SN simulations and in the description of the Milky Way magnetic field, we revisit the bounds on magnetic dipole moments. We find for Dirac electron neutrinos $\mu_{\nu_e} \lesssim 4.8 \times 10^{-13} \mu_B$, superseding all existing terrestrial and astrophysical constraints.

hep-ph.title: Active Galactic Nuclei as Beyond the Standard Model Laboratories: a White Paper
hep-ph.author: Gonzalo Herrera, Filippo Sala, Piero Ullio, Misty C. Bentz, Carlos Blanco, Roberto Caiozzo, Marina Cermeño, Matteo Cerruti, James M. Cline, Andrea Giovanni De Marchi, Pierfrancesco Di Cintio, Alessandro Granelli, R. Andrew Gustafson, Bradley J. Kavanagh, Cristina Lagunas Gualda, Kohta Murase, Takuya Okawa, Xavier Rodrigues, Lorenzo Ubaldi, Gabrijela Zaharijas
hep-ph.abstract: Multi-messenger and multi-wavelength observations of Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) can provide otherwise inaccessible knowledge about physics Beyond the Standard Model (BSM), and may even lead to its discovery. Realizing this potential hinges on two parallel efforts: advancing our understanding of AGN and of the dark matter around them, and identifying the BSM signatures that are at once promising and robust against the gaps in that understanding. These fields have attracted growing interest in recent years, also motivated by the IceCube association of neutrinos to individual AGN, yet we have only begun to explore their cross-fertilization. This white paper offers a new perspective on this interdisciplinary endeavor. It concisely reviews the state of the art in each field and at their interface, and identifies the key open questions that must be addressed to strengthen our prospects for learning about BSM physics with AGN.

hep-ph.title: Thermal Composite Dark Matter at LZ
hep-ph.author: Dario Buttazzo, Andrea Di Lecce, Roberto Franceschini, Giulio Marino, Paolo Panci
hep-ph.abstract: We show that stable fermionic resonances of Composite Higgs models provide a thermal inelastic Dark Matter interpretation of the high-energy nuclear-recoil event LZ230616. Their stability follows from an exact accidental parity of the strong sector. Annihilation channels from composite interactions link the thermal relic mass to the strong coupling, allowing masses well beyond the pure electroweak prediction. We identify three scenarios in which the neutral states form a split pseudo-Dirac pair, distinguished by the origin of the inelastic coupling to the $Z$ boson. In the pure electroweak regime, the pair consists of the neutral components of a complex Higgsino-like doublet. Its unsuppressed inelastic $Z$ coupling requires Dark Matter masses above 20 TeV. In the pure strong regime, the suppressed $Z$ coupling of neutral states with vanishing hypercharge arises from strong interactions alone, allowing for smaller splittings and TeV-scale masses. In the third regime, which interpolates between the previous two, the neutral components of multiplets with different hypercharge are mixed. This enhances their inelastic coupling, accommodating the LZ event for masses of a few TeV and splittings around 300 keV, with mixing angles of order $10^\circ$. All three cases provide a thermal Dark Matter candidate able to explain the LZ event, consistently with the solar-capture bounds, the LZ high-energy sideband, and gamma-ray indirect searches.

hep-ph.title: Smuggling baryon asymmetry through strong washout
hep-ph.author: Kåre Fridell, Michal Malinský, Javier Perez-Soler
hep-ph.abstract: We propose a scheme in which a primordial net baryon number generated at or around the unification scale may survive subsequent strong washout phases associated with active sphalerons and interactions of right-handed neutrinos inherent to thermal leptogenesis. A simple realization of this, namely, a long-lived scalar population injecting the net $B-L$ it carries into the Standard Model matter sector late enough to be safe from a strong washout, is constructed and studied in the context of a simple Pati-Salam scalar sector with a heavy $SU(4)_C$ sextet scalar.

hep-ph.title: Perturbative QCD Analysis for the Electric Dipole Moment of $Ξ$ and $Σ$ Hyperons from CP-Violating Dipole Interactions
hep-ph.author: Xi-Yu Mu, Kai-Bao Chen, Jian-Ping Ma, Xuan-Bo Tong
hep-ph.abstract: Hyperon electric dipole moments (EDMs) probe CP-violating interactions beyond the Standard Model. Motivated by the recent BESIII measurement [Ablikim et al., Science 393, 1027] and the perturbative QCD analysis of the $\Lambda$ EDM form factor $d_\Lambda$ [Chen et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 051902], we extend the perturbative QCD calculation of the EDM form factor to the $\Xi$ and $\Sigma$ hyperons. We derive factorization formulas from quark EDM and chromoelectric dipole moment contributions in terms of leading-twist light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs). Using lattice-QCD results for the LCDAs and the strange-quark dipole moment ranges inferred from the BESIII $d_\Lambda$ bound and neutron EDM constraints, we obtain the conditional estimates $-4.8 \times 10^{-18} < d_{\Xi^-} < 1.8\times10^{-18}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $-6.1\times10^{-19} < d_{\Sigma^+} < 2.4\times10^{-19}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$ at the scale of ${J/\psi}$ mass. Dedicated searches at BESIII and the future Super Tau-Charm Factory could further constrain these quark-level sources of CP violation.

hep-ph.title: Analytic next-to-leading order electroweak corrections to Higgs boson pair production in the forward limit
hep-ph.author: Joshua Davies, Dominik Grau, Kay Schönwald, Matthias Steinhauser, Daniel Stremmer
hep-ph.abstract: We calculate next-to-leading order electroweak corrections for Higgs boson pair production in the gluon fusion channel, in the forward limit. We perform an analytic calculation and obtain a final result for the partonic cross section that depends explicitly on all kinematic parameters and particle masses. We describe our method, which can be readily applied to similar processes. We observe rapid convergence within the validity range of the forward expansion. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the entire phase space can be covered when this approach is combined with the high-energy expansion.

hep-ph.title: A new angle on coherence-violating logarithms in color-singlet processes
hep-ph.author: Mrinal Dasgupta, Alexander Fraley, Pier Francesco Monni, Saad Nabeebaccus
hep-ph.abstract: We introduce a new formulation for the resummation of coherence-violating logarithms for the transverse energy flow in rapidity gaps in the Drell-Yan process. Our formalism allows us to resum coherence-violating logarithms in the gap cross section in the phenomenologically important regime where the gap size is comparable to the logarithm of the transverse energy. In the formal small gap limit, our result reduces to the known state-of-the-art resummation of coherence-violating logarithms for the Drell-Yan process. However, we identify sizable new corrections even for moderate gap widths that significantly modify the phenomenological picture for LHC applications. This work will form an important element of future extensions to a range of global and non-global observables.

hep-ph.title: $B\to K a$ decays in QCD factorization and revised bounds on ALP couplings
hep-ph.author: Upalaparna Banerjee, Cristhian Calderon, Matthias Neubert
hep-ph.abstract: Rare flavor-changing processes such as $B\to K a$ offer sensitive probes of axion-like particles (ALPs) for masses below a few GeV. We study this process in the framework of QCD factorization and ALP effective theory, in which the ALP couples to the Standard Model (SM) fermions through shift-invariant derivative interactions. In contrast to previous studies, where flavor violation arises solely from flavor-changing ALP couplings, we also include the contributions proportional to flavor-conserving ALP couplings, in which the flavor change is mediated by the weak interactions of the SM. Based on this analysis, we derive upper bounds on both flavor-changing and flavor-conserving ALP couplings at low energies. Then we consider the UV scenario of a "minimally flavor-violating ALP", which features flavor-universal ALP-fermion couplings at very high energies, and evaluate the resulting constraints on the UV couplings.

hep-ph.title: On the Structure of the Nuclear-Clock Isotope $^{229}$Th Beyond Quadratic Order
hep-ph.author: Chaja Baruch, Doron Gazit, Hans-Werner Hammer, Fiona Kirk, Joachim Kopp, Gil Paz, Ekkehard Peik, Gilad Perez, Yotam Soreq, Konstantin Springmann
hep-ph.abstract: Precision measurements of the exceptionally low-energy nuclear transition of $^{229}$Th, offer an extraordinary sensitivity to a variety of new light fields. However, interpreting such measurements requires nuclear-structure information beyond what is currently constrained by spectroscopy. We develop a systematic description of the electric multipole interactions governing the hyperfine structure of ${}^{229}$Th, including the hexadecapole contribution, and perform a symmetry-based analysis of the resulting hyperfine splittings in crystalline environments. Hyperfine spectroscopy generally constrains combinations of nuclear moments and crystal-field gradients, leading to degeneracies when higher multipole interactions are allowed. We then combine experimental nuclear observables, particle-rotor relations, and a deformed-Fermi charge-density model to investigate the electromagnetic contribution to the nuclear clock's sensitivity to variations in the fine-structure constant. We find that higher-order nuclear deformation and state-dependent differences in the radial charge distribution of the clock states can substantially alter the predicted sensitivity, introducing large uncertainties that are not constrained by existing measurements. Our results highlight the importance of combining nuclear and solid-state theory with complementary measurements, including spectroscopy of higher-spin states, to constrain the nuclear structure and improve predictions of the clock's sensitivity to new physics. Our symmetry-based analysis also provides a framework for using hyperfine spectroscopy to investigate local defect symmetries in crystalline hosts.

hep-ph.title: Probing scalar-mediated Lorentz violation with hydrogen masers and spin-precession of molecules
hep-ph.author: Djuna Croon, Tanmay Kumar Poddar
hep-ph.abstract: We propose using hydrogen maser spectroscopy and molecular spin-precession experiments, traditionally employed in precision frequency measurements and searches for the electron electric dipole moment, as complementary probes of light scalar-mediated, spin-dependent fifth forces. We investigate their sensitivity to Lorentz-violating interactions mediated by scalars with masses ranging from $\mathcal{O}(10^{-4}~\mu\mathrm{eV})$ to $\mathcal{O}(10~\mathrm{keV})$. While hydrogen maser spectroscopy and molecular spin-precession measurements probe different combinations of Lorentz-violating couplings, we find that the strongest projected sensitivities can be achieved using spin-precession of ultracold molecules, benefiting from their extended coherence times. These experimental approaches provide access to previously unexplored regions of parameter space, probing interaction ranges extending from centimeter to sub-angstrom scales. Our proposals highlight the potential of precision atomic and molecular experiments to search for new spin-dependent scalar-mediated interactions and violations of fundamental spacetime symmetries.

hep-ph.title: Probing $τ$ lepton dipole moments at multi-TeV muon colliders
hep-ph.author: Dario Buttazzo, Gabriele Levati, Yang Ma, Fabio Maltoni, Paride Paradisi, ZeQiang Wang
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate the sensitivity of future multi-TeV muon colliders to the electromagnetic and weak dipole moments of the $\tau$ lepton within the dimension-six Standard Model Effective Field Theory. We consider $\tau^+\tau^-$ production through $\mu^+\mu^-$ annihilation and vector-boson scattering, electroweak-boson-associated $\tau$ production, and the radiative Higgs decay $H\to\tau^+\tau^-\gamma$. At high energies, the dipole-induced contributions quadratic in the Wilson coefficients become particularly important, with associated Higgs production, $\mu^+\mu^-\to\tau^+\tau^-H$, providing the strongest sensitivity through energy-enhanced contact interactions. The remaining channels offer complementary probes of the underlying dipole operators. For a $10$~TeV muon collider with an integrated luminosity of $10\,\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$, we obtain combined sensitivities at the nominal $95\%$ confidence level of $|\Delta a_\tau|<1.2\times10^{-5}$, $|d_\tau|<6.6\times10^{-20}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$, $|\Delta a_\tau^Z|<1.8\times10^{-5}$, and $|d_\tau^Z|<1.0\times10^{-19}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$. Compared with FCC-ee projections, the muon collider offers substantially stronger sensitivity to the electric dipole moments, while both facilities offer complementary probes of magnetic dipole moments. These results motivate further studies incorporating realistic detector effects and systematic uncertainties.

hep-ph.title: Double parton scattering singularities in two-loop gluon-fusion amplitudes
hep-ph.author: Arunima Bhattacharya
hep-ph.abstract: Gluon fusion to two massive colour singlets can develop a double parton scattering (DPS) singularity as $p_T\to0$: each gluon splits, and its daughters fuse pairwise. We determine two-loop logarithms using a common kernel and derive finite matching functions analytically for gluon and quark splittings. Normalised to one loop, the cubic coefficient changes sign between channels. Complete $gg\to HH$, $gg\to AA$ and $gg\to ZZ$ amplitudes confirm the predicted colour, helicity and parity dependence and phase. The kernel gives leading DPS logarithms for other pairs with this DPS configuration.

hep-ph.title: Flavor Entanglement as a CPT Violation Witness in Neutrino Oscillations
hep-ph.author: Bipin Singh Koranga, Biswmkwr Boro, Vivek Kumar Nautiyal

hep-ph.title: Top-Quark Physics after Evidence for Toponium
hep-ph.author: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger
hep-ph.abstract: The top quark decays before it hadronizes, and toponium, the t\bar t bound state, was long thought unobservable as a resonance. CMS and ATLAS each report an excess of top-quark pairs at threshold, above five standard deviations over fixed-order quantum chromodynamics (QCD), and CMS confirms it in a second decay channel. Its angular distributions match the color-singlet pseudoscalar quasi-bound state \eta_t of nonrelativistic QCD, although an additional pseudoscalar boson is not excluded and higher-order fixed-order QCD accounts for part of the enhancement. We review the theory, ATLAS's nominal Green's-function signal model, and the measurements, whose cross sections range from about 3 to 13 pb. Part of the spread comes from the signal model and part persists between analyses using the same model. We discuss consequences for entanglement, the top mass, and heavy-pseudoscalar searches. We then review the top-quark program, from mass definitions to electroweak precision, flavor, the charge-conjugation and parity (CP) structure of the top Yukawa coupling, supersymmetry, multi-top production, and effective field theory. We close with prospects at the High-Luminosity LHC and future colliders, where an e^+e^- threshold scan can determine the top-quark mass in a short-distance scheme to a few tens of MeV.

hep-ph.title: Triangle singularity with different dynamical couplings
hep-ph.author: Jun Wang, Xiao-Hai Liu, Qiang Zhao
hep-ph.abstract: We carry out a systematic study of the impact of dynamical couplings of the vertices on the manifestations of the triangle singularity (TS) in the loop amplitude. Twelve combinations of external and internal spin-parity quantum numbers, covering the $PPS$, $VPP$, $VVP$, $VPA$, $VVV$, $VVA$, and $VVS$ effective vertices, are enumerated. Each loop amplitude is reduced via the Passarino--Veltman decomposition into scalar integrals $A_{0}$, $B_{0}$, and $C_{0}$, whose Lorentz-scalar coefficients encode the dynamical content of the vertices. Using the masses and kinematics of the $\eta(1405)\to\pi^{+}\pi^{-}\pi^{0}$ transition via the $K^{*}\bar{K}K$ loop with the intermediate $f_{0}(980)$ resonance in the $\pi^+\pi^-$ invariant spectrum as a common numerical benchmark for the twelve spin-parity assignments, we find that the same loop topology produces three distinct phenomena which manifest through the lineshapes, i.e. a narrow peak dominated by the $C_{0}$ contribution; a suppressed peak in which the $B_{0}$ and $C_{0}$ function contributions are comparable; and a cusp-like profile in which the coefficient of the leading Landau logarithm vanishes at the physical TS point. These results indicate that the visibility of a TS enhancement is not fixed by the Landau condition alone but reshaped by the detailed dynamics involved in the loop transitions.

hep-ph.title: An exact separability criterion for the $J/ψΛ$ spin state in $Λ_b^0\to J/ψ\,Λ$ decays at the LHC
hep-ph.author: Yujie Li, Xiaofan Hu, Liming Zhang
hep-ph.abstract: We derive an exact separability criterion for the spin state of the $J/\psi\Lambda$ pair produced in $\Lambda_b^0\to J/\psi(\to\mu^+\mu^-)\,\Lambda(\to p\pi^-)$ decays, taking into account the $\Lambda_b^0$ polarization at the LHC. Within the four-amplitude family $\{a_\pm,b_\pm\}$, the system is separable if and only if $(1+P_b\cos\theta)a_+b_+=(1-P_b\cos\theta)a_-b_-=P_b\sin\theta b_+b_-=0$, where $\theta$ is the $\Lambda$ production angle defined in the LHC environment. We propose a profiled likelihood ratio test to probe entanglement in the full five-dimensional angular analysis. Idealized pseudoexperiments compare this test with a negativity test and a test based on the angular moments $M_7$ and $M_9$ for rejecting the $a_+=b_-=0$ hypothesis. At both $3\sigma$ and $5\sigma$ significance, the proposed test achieves a $90\%$ rejection power with about half as many signal events as the other two methods. These results support the prospects for entanglement evidence with samples on the existing scale and for observation with larger samples.

hep-ph.title: Millicharged Fermions as Dark Matter: Theoretical Modeling and Experimental Detection
hep-ph.author: Momchil Naydenov
hep-ph.abstract: Fermions with a small effective charge, $\qeff\ll1$, arise from kinetic mixing between an unbroken (or nearly unbroken) dark $U(1)'$ and electromagnetism, or from a genuinely fractional charge. Millicharged particles (mCPs) inherit the Pauli-exclusion constraints on fermionic dark matter (DM) in galaxies, while adding a long-range plasma phenomenology absent for neutral candidates. This review connects three strands: (i) the symmetry structure, cosmology and astrophysical bounds of millicharged fermions, comparing kinetic-mixing and fractional-charge realizations; (ii) the role of mCPs in galactic halo formation and dynamics, and when they fit the Ruffini--Argüelles--Rueda (RAR) self-gravitating core--halo model; and (iii) experimental techniques for detecting mCPs trapped on Earth, arriving from the galactic halo, or emitted by the Sun. We show that a collisionless halo of keV--MeV millicharged fermions requires $\alpha'\lesssim7\times10^{-13}$--$2\times10^{-10}$, depending on mass and velocity, orders of magnitude below the coupling needed for thermal freeze-out via $\chi\bar\chi\to A'A'$ in the Milky Way and dwarf galaxies. A RAR halo made of the mCP itself thus needs non-thermal production, a charge-symmetric plasma and very small dark coupling, whereas a sub-dominant mCP component can be added without changing the halo. We close with open theoretical and experimental challenges and a summary of the allowed mCP parameter space.

hep-ph.title: Scalar inelastic scattering of pseudo-Majorana dark matter through a radion portal
hep-ph.author: Ruifeng Leng, Kirtimaan A. Mohan, Keping Xie, Hong-Hao Zhang
hep-ph.abstract: We investigate a radion portal for pseudo-Majorana dark matter as an interpretation of the high-recoil event LZ230616. In contrast to the familiar pseudo-Dirac regime, the pseudo-Majorana structure allows a dominant scalar transition while suppressing elastic scattering. Endothermic kinematics remove low-energy recoils, while the nuclear response shapes the surviving high-recoil spectrum. Combining the accepted LZ event count with the Born-level thermal relic abundance yields a reference solution with $m_\chi=1$ TeV, $\delta=340$ keV, and $m_r=30$ GeV. This solution lies within the published LZ spin-independent $\mathcal{O}_1^s$ interval and remains compatible with existing OPAL and CMS constraints, while a simplified HL-LHC diphoton projection could probe it. Solar neutrino searches offer a complementary test. The benchmark's energetic-daughter proxy rates are comparable in magnitude to the rate scales reconstructed from IceCube's direct $b\bar{b}$ and $\tau^+\tau^-$ templates. An illustrative IceCube-Gen2 rescaling suggests future sensitivity, while a model-specific assessment requires the radion-cascade neutrino spectra and detector response.

hep-ph.title: Universal Mass Equation for Equal-Quantum Excited-States Sets~III
hep-ph.author: L. David Roper(VTech), Igor Strakovsky(GWU)
hep-ph.abstract: Using our simple logarithmic Universal Mass Equation, we considered heavy non-$q\bar{q}$ meson states. PDG2026 reported a series of mesons with quantum numbers not allowed for standard $q\bar{q}$ states. Using LQCD predictions, we evaluated a scalar $0^{++}$ and tensor $2^{++}$ glueball series for which predictions are available. This approach allows us to predict heavy states that require future experimental studies. Additionally, we consider the possible misidentification of some meson states.

hep-ph.title: A Universal Axion in a Twin-QCD Sector
hep-ph.author: Stuart Raby, Scott Watson
hep-ph.abstract: Dark matter may consist of multiple components with distinct particle-physics origins. We investigate a scenario in which a universal axion couples to both visible and twin QCD, with twin baryons providing a possible dominant dark-matter component. The presence of a second strongly interacting sector can substantially enhance the axion mass while preserving its role in resolving the strong-CP problem, provided the physical vacuum angles are appropriately aligned. For a representative uniformly rescaled twin spectrum with a confinement scale five times that of ordinary QCD, the axion mass is enhanced by approximately a factor of 25.Using lattice-informed QCD results and a two-temperature description of the early universe, we investigate the cosmological evolution and relative abundances of the dark-sector components. In a representative conditional numerical benchmark, axions account for a small percentage of the observed dark matter, while twin baryons could constitute the remainder for a suitable primordial baryon asymmetry. We also examine the implications for additional relativistic species, strong-CP alignment, and the interactions of stable twin matter.Our results provide a quantitative framework for exploring mixed axion--twin-baryon dark matter and identify the particle-physics and cosmological conditions necessary for a viable realization, including constraints from the thermal history and formation of cosmic structure.

hep-ph.title: Loop-induced $gg\to ZH$ at NLO+PS for LHC simulations: exact, fast scale and PDF event weights, theory uncertainties, and the limits of rescaled LO+PS
hep-ph.author: Licheng Zhang, Christopher Palmer
hep-ph.abstract: We study loop-induced $gg\to ZH$ production with charged-lepton and neutrino $Z$ decays at next-to-leading order (NLO) in QCD matched to parton showers, using public software at $\sqrt{s}=13$ and 13.6 TeV. An exact loop-amplitude cache reduces event-generation time by a factor of 26 with 450 scale and PDF weights, while Born suppression improves boosted-event statistics without changing the weighted prediction. We present inclusive results for both channels and charged-lepton differential and STXS Stage 1.3 predictions with theory uncertainties. At 13.6 TeV, fixed-order top-quark mass-scheme variations transferred to NLO+PS dominate the statistically precise central-Higgs STXS bins for $p_\mathrm{T}^V\ge150$ GeV, reaching 32-50%. An inclusive $K$ factor does not reproduce the boosted and jet-dependent NLO+PS spectra of the tested LO+PS samples, and the differences depend strongly on the shower prescription. For specified CMS- and ATLAS-style vetoed sources at 13.6 TeV, we construct separate charged-lepton and neutrino corrections using ensembles of gradient-boosted classifiers, with calibration, target-theory variations and transfer uncertainties. Independent tests show substantial improvement over inclusive rescaling in most tested distributions, but not uniform closure. In charged-lepton calibration comparisons, the median STXS uncertainty from transported NLO scales and transfer terms is 17% for both the CMS- and ATLAS-style corrections, compared with LO scale uncertainties of 28% and 26% at fixed $K$. These comparisons do not include the complete target-theory budget. The corrections do not restore the depleted hard-recoil population; the highest ATLAS-style $p_\mathrm{T}^H$ bin stays below NLO+PS even at the upper edge of its band. The setup, reference results, and source- and channel-specific models support new NLO+PS generation and reuse of existing samples within stated limits.

hep-ph.title: Imprints of Non-local Top-Higgs Interaction on Loop Induced Higgs Processes
hep-ph.author: Avik Banerjee, Rohan Pramanick, Tirtha Sankar Ray
hep-ph.abstract: A composite Higgs arising from an underlying strong sector generally has non-local interactions with the elementary sector, formulated in terms of momentum-dependent form factors. We construct the minimal Ball-Chiu-type vertices consistent with gauge-invariant non-local $\bar{t}th$ couplings containing Wilson lines, where recursive Ward-Takahashi identities connect the Yukawa interaction to higher-order contact interactions. For a symmetric monopole form factor motivated by lowest-resonance dominance, we compute the top-loop contributions to $gg \to h$ and $h \to \gamma\gamma$ amplitudes in closed form, and demonstrate a logarithmically enhanced deviation from the Standard Model. Current measurements at the LHC exclude the characteristic new physics scale below 3.6 TeV at $2\sigma$, while future colliders could extend the sensitivity to approximately 8 TeV.
