hep-th.abstract: In quantum gravity the algebra of observables of a subregion is of type III$_1$ at leading order in the semiclassical expansion, and it becomes of type II once the gravitational constraint is imposed. Hence generalized entropy acquires a trace, however it is defined only up to an additive constant. In this work we argue that in four-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity this constant is the Gauss--Bonnet contribution to the Wald entropy, and that it is carried by the normalization of the trace and not by the state. In particular, the conical expansion of the Gauss--Bonnet density is exactly linear in the deficit angle, and on smooth squashed cones it reduces to the intrinsic curvature of the cut, so that the term is a constant on every smooth cross-section and carries no boost energy. Its Noether charge is invariant under all deformations within a topological sector and central in any algebra that preserves the sector, and thus a state-independent constant on such an algebra can only rescale the trace. Additionally, when the boundary of the subregion is completed as the Euler action requires, the Gauss--Bonnet term does not contribute to the presymplectic form, the crossed product is inherited from Einstein gravity, and the constant is the Euler number of the excised Euclidean tip. We state the hypotheses, we weaken factoriality to a central decomposition, and we illustrate the mechanism in Jackiw--Teitelboim gravity and in topological black holes in anti-de Sitter space, where the topological weight displaces the Hawking--Page temperature and a black-hole merger shifts the coarse-grained boundary entropy by a state-independent amount.

hep-th.title: Axion electrodynamics and the advection-diffusion structure of TEM modes in hollow-conductor waveguides
hep-th.author: André H. Gomes
hep-th.abstract: We present a systematic investigation of transverse electromagnetic (TEM) modes in hollow-conductor waveguides filled with a dielectric medium described by axion electrodynamics. While such modes do not propagate in conventional single-conductor waveguides, the coupling of the axion field to an external magnetic field enables their propagation. We show that the resulting TEM modes are governed by an advection-diffusion-type equation for the transverse electrostatic potential, establishing a direct mathematical connection between axion electrodynamics and advection-diffusion phenomena. We illustrate this connection through explicit solutions and field profiles for cylindrical waveguides, considering uniform and rigid rotational drift fields, both individually and in combination, as well as different values of the parameter controlling the advection-to-diffusion ratio (Péclet number). These results establish a transport-based framework for understanding how spatial variations of the axion-electrodynamics background shape the transverse electromagnetic fields in hollow-conductor waveguides.

hep-th.title: Scalar inelastic scattering of pseudo-Majorana dark matter through a radion portal
hep-th.author: Ruifeng Leng, Kirtimaan A. Mohan, Keping Xie, Hong-Hao Zhang
hep-th.abstract: We investigate a radion portal for pseudo-Majorana dark matter as an interpretation of the high-recoil event LZ230616. In contrast to the familiar pseudo-Dirac regime, the pseudo-Majorana structure allows a dominant scalar transition while suppressing elastic scattering. Endothermic kinematics remove low-energy recoils, while the nuclear response shapes the surviving high-recoil spectrum. Combining the accepted LZ event count with the Born-level thermal relic abundance yields a reference solution with $m_\chi=1$ TeV, $\delta=340$ keV, and $m_r=30$ GeV. This solution lies within the published LZ spin-independent $\mathcal{O}_1^s$ interval and remains compatible with existing OPAL and CMS constraints, while a simplified HL-LHC diphoton projection could probe it. Solar neutrino searches offer a complementary test. The benchmark's energetic-daughter proxy rates are comparable in magnitude to the rate scales reconstructed from IceCube's direct $b\bar{b}$ and $\tau^+\tau^-$ templates. An illustrative IceCube-Gen2 rescaling suggests future sensitivity, while a model-specific assessment requires the radion-cascade neutrino spectra and detector response.

hep-th.title: Entanglement cost and classical capacity of multimode Gaussian states and channels
hep-th.author: Yuan Gao, Gerardo Adesso
hep-th.abstract: Gaussian states and operations are central to continuous-variable quantum information and communication. For systems with any finite number of modes, we prove that entanglement of formation, Gaussian entanglement of formation, and entanglement cost coincide for every finite-energy bipartite Gaussian state. Their common value is strongly superadditive and lower-bounds entanglement of formation and entanglement cost for arbitrary non-Gaussian states with the same covariance matrix. We then determine the entanglement cost of every multimode Gaussian channel as well as its classical capacity under a mean energy constraint. These quantities reduce to Gaussian covariance optimizations, and the capacity is attained by pure Gaussian signals with Gaussian displacement modulation, independently across channel uses. The proof combines geodesic convexity of entanglement for pure Gaussian states with a relative-entropy inequality for arbitrary states. We also obtain a closed formula for the entanglement cost of a family of four-mode bound entangled states.

hep-th.title: Non-Invertible Quantum Cellular Automata I: Microscopic Definition of Non-Invertible Symmetries
hep-th.author: Sahand Seifnashri, Shu-Heng Shao
hep-th.abstract: We introduce non-invertible quantum cellular automata (QCAs), defined as locality-preserving quantum channels that are dualizable and pure. This provides an operator-algebraic definition of non-invertible symmetries of quantum lattice systems, formulated in terms of their action on local operators. Focusing on quantum spin chains, we motivate these defining conditions and conjecture that every such quantum channel admits a realization by dualizable topological defects or, equivalently, by dualizable sequential quantum circuits. We construct a broad class of examples, including on-site non-invertible symmetries that are anomalous, as well as higher-dimensional examples. In Part II of this work, we reconstruct topological defects whose boundary algebras yield an index theory that classifies non-invertible QCAs up to blend equivalence.

hep-th.title: A Universal Axion in a Twin-QCD Sector
hep-th.author: Stuart Raby, Scott Watson
hep-th.abstract: Dark matter may consist of multiple components with distinct particle-physics origins. We investigate a scenario in which a universal axion couples to both visible and twin QCD, with twin baryons providing a possible dominant dark-matter component. The presence of a second strongly interacting sector can substantially enhance the axion mass while preserving its role in resolving the strong-CP problem, provided the physical vacuum angles are appropriately aligned. For a representative uniformly rescaled twin spectrum with a confinement scale five times that of ordinary QCD, the axion mass is enhanced by approximately a factor of 25.Using lattice-informed QCD results and a two-temperature description of the early universe, we investigate the cosmological evolution and relative abundances of the dark-sector components. In a representative conditional numerical benchmark, axions account for a small percentage of the observed dark matter, while twin baryons could constitute the remainder for a suitable primordial baryon asymmetry. We also examine the implications for additional relativistic species, strong-CP alignment, and the interactions of stable twin matter.Our results provide a quantitative framework for exploring mixed axion--twin-baryon dark matter and identify the particle-physics and cosmological conditions necessary for a viable realization, including constraints from the thermal history and formation of cosmic structure.

hep-th.title: Zero mode surface of Hermitian two-by-two matrices
hep-th.author: Andreas Sykora
hep-th.abstract: We classify the zero mode surfaces, also called Clifford spectra, of Hermitian $2\times 2$ matrices. Using the covariance of the Dirac operator under the Euclidean group and its invariance under unitary conjugation, together with a singular value decomposition, every $m$-tuple of Hermitian $2\times 2$ matrices, after adjoining zero matrices if $m<3$, is reduced to the normal form $(b_1\sigma_1,b_2\sigma_2,b_3\sigma_3,0,\dots,0)$ with $b_1\geq b_2\geq b_3\geq 0$. Since adding a vanishing matrix only embeds the Clifford spectrum into a higher-dimensional space, it suffices to consider three matrices. In this normal form the determinant of the Dirac operator is given in closed form and its critical points are determined explicitly. The zero mode surface consists of one or two points if $b_3=0$. Otherwise it consists of two disjoint topological spheres if $b_1>b_2+b_3$, of two topological spheres touching at one point if $b_1=b_2+b_3$, and of a single topological sphere if $b_1<b_2+b_3$. The topology is thus governed by the triangle inequality for $(b_1,b_2,b_3)$, which can be interpreted with Heron's formula. In particular, the Clifford spectrum of any tuple of Hermitian $2\times 2$ matrices is never empty.

hep-th.title: Convergence of the quasinormal-mode expansion of the Kerr Green function
hep-th.author: Davide Ciattaglia, Adrien Kuntz, Enrico Barausse
hep-th.abstract: Black-hole ringdown is usually modeled as a linear superposition of quasinormal modes, and fits to gravitational-wave observations increasingly include high overtones. However, the overtone sum does not necessarily converge: overtones are more strongly damped and thus decay faster in time, but their amplitudes in the Green function (the signal at an observer produced by an impulse at a source point) grow, so the mode description may break down before a finite time. We show that for a rotating (Kerr) black hole this time has a clear geometric meaning. For highly damped modes, the amplitudes grow exponentially with the optical distance from the source and the observer to a characteristic "bounce" radius close to the black hole, defined as the location where the mode amplitude is smallest. For one family of modes, the amplitudes are also suppressed the farther the source and observer sit from the equatorial plane. Rotation therefore makes the onset of convergence depend on direction as well as distance, extending the geometric picture from bounce radii to bounce surfaces. Combining these effects gives a sufficient condition for absolute convergence. For spin $a/M = 0.7$, we map how this time varies with source and observer position, and amplitudes computed numerically reproduce the predicted spatial dependence to better than one percent. These results set geometric limits on when the quasinormal-mode sums converge.

hep-th.title: Complete Cosmological Collider Signatures from Right-handed Neutrino Loops
hep-th.author: Linghao Song, Jingtao You, Ming Cheng, Hong-Jian He, Xingang Chen
hep-th.abstract: We study the complete cosmological collider (CC) signatures from right-handed neutrino loops with chemical-potential enhancement. These CC signals are induced by the inflaton-right-handed-neutrino interaction and can be extracted in the collinear squeezed configuration, which allows the right-handed-neutrino triangle loop to be factorized into the hard and soft parts. We precisely compute the soft part of the fermion loop for the first time by using the complete mode functions and the full loop integral, and treat the hard part as a tree-level subdiagram. We subtract the large-momentum asymptotic terms of the soft loop integrand and retain their finite contributions to the oscillation. We then evaluate the full spinor-helicity and Schwinger-Keldysh sums to obtain a finite, closed analytic formula for the complex clock coefficient. We further derive a compact formula for the leading CC signals in the large-chemical-potential expansion. We analyze the structure of the soft-part contribution by examining the sum of residues of the Mellin poles of the fermion propagators. For this, we demonstrate that the first local pole on each soft line contributes half of the asymptotic coefficient on one Schwinger-Keldysh path and the remaining local poles on the second soft line supply the other half.

hep-th.title: Holographic covering and the fortuity of black holes
hep-th.author: Chi-Ming Chang, Ying-Hsuan Lin
hep-th.abstract: We propose a classification of BPS states in holographic CFTs into monotone and fortuitous, based on their behaviors in the large $N$ limit. Intuitively, monotone BPS states form infinite sequences with increasing rank $N$, while fortuitous ones exist within finite ranges of consecutive ranks. A precise definition is formulated using supercharge cohomology. We conjecture that under the AdS/CFT correspondence, monotone BPS states are dual to smooth horizonless geometries, and fortuitous ones are responsible for typical black hole microstates and give dominant contributions to the entropy. We present supporting evidence for our conjectures in the ${\cal N}=4$ SYM and symmetric product orbifolds.

hep-th.title: Equivalence Relations on Vertex Operator Algebras, II: Witt Equivalence and Orbifolds
hep-th.author: Sven Möller, Brandon C. Rayhaun
hep-th.abstract: When can two strongly rational vertex operator algebras or 1+1d rational conformal field theories (RCFTs) be related by topological manipulations? For vertex operator algebras, the term "topological manipulations" refers to operations like passing to a conformal extension or restricting to a conformal subalgebra; for RCFTs, topological manipulations include operations like gauging (or orbifolding) a finite part of a generalized global symmetry or interpolating to a new theory via a topological line interface of finite quantum dimension.Inspired by results in the theory of even lattices and tensor categories, we say that two strongly rational vertex operator algebras are Witt equivalent if their central charges agree and if their modular tensor categories are Witt equivalent. Two RCFTs are said to be Witt equivalent if their central charges agree and if their associated 2+1d topological field theories can be separated by a topological surface. We argue that Witt equivalence is necessary for two theories to be related by topological manipulations. We conjecture that it is also sufficient, and give proofs in various special cases.We relate this circle of ideas to the problem of classifying RCFTs, and to lore concerning deformation classes of quantum field theories. We use the notion of Witt equivalence to argue, conditional on a mild technical hypothesis, that all of the finite symmetries of the $\mathrm{SU}(2)_1$ Wess-Zumino-Witten model are invertible. We also sketch a "quantum Galois theory" for chiral CFTs, which generalizes prior mathematical literature by incorporating non-invertible symmetries; we illustrate this non-invertible Galois theory in the context of the monster CFT $V^\natural$, for which we produce two Fibonacci lines. Finally, we discuss $p$-neighborhood of vertex operator algebras, which is a special topological manipulation related to $\mathbb{Z}_p$-orbifolding.

hep-th.title: Analytic approaches to anisotropic holographic superfluids in asymptotically hyperscaling violation geometry
hep-th.author: Gitae Kim, Yeong Seok Choi, Jae-Hyuk Oh
hep-th.abstract: We explore anisotropic holographic superfluidity and find analytic solutions near critical point where superfluid/normalfluid phase transition appears in a holographic dual fluid system. In arXiv:hep-th/1109.4592, the authors obtained such an analytic solution in 5-dimensional Einstein-SU(2)Yang-Mills system, and it is asymptotically AdS$_5$. What is more in this note is that we get analytic solutions near the critical point in 3- and 4- dimensional Einstein-Scalar-U(1)$\times$SU(2)Yang-Mills systems, which become asymptotically hyperscaling violation geometry. We also get leading order back reactions to the background geometry, which clearly shows spatial anisotropy of the bulk geometry. To explore the properties of the spacetime, we compute holographic entanglement entropy and confirm that the superfluid/normalfluid phase transition must occur at the critical point.

hep-th.title: Small-$b$ expansion of the DOZZ formula for light operators
hep-th.author: Franco Ferrari, Marcin R. Piatek, Artur R. Pietrykowski
hep-th.abstract: We present a systematic asymptotic small-$b$ expansion of the Liouville DOZZ three-point structure constant in the light-operator regime $\alpha_i=b\sigma_i$ in the limit $b\to0$. In this limit, the DOZZ structure constant admits the asymptotic representation \[ C(b\sigma_1,b\sigma_2,b\sigma_3) \sim {\cal P}(b;\sigma_i) \left[ 1+\sum_{n\ge1}b^{2n}\Omega_n(\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3) \right], \qquad b\to0 , \] where ${\cal P}(b;\sigma_i)$ is an explicitly determined prefactor. Using Thorn's asymptotic expansion of the $\Upsilon_b$-function, we derive explicit closed-form expressions for the first coefficients $\Omega_n(\sigma_i)$ and show that they form a symmetric polynomial structure in the variables $\sigma_i$. The resulting asymptotic expansion provides explicit finite-$b$ corrections to the leading light-limit Liouville three-point data and furnishes a practical framework for applications in celestial holography. In particular, it provides Liouville data relevant for a perturbative program aimed at studying finite-$b$ corrections to celestial Yang-Mills amplitudes. Finally, we formulate such a perturbative Liouville framework and discuss several directions for its future development.

hep-th.title: BPS Solutions of 4d Euclidean N=2 Supergravity with Higher Derivative Interactions
hep-th.author: Soumya Adhikari, Abhinava Bhattacharjee, Amitabh Virmani
hep-th.abstract: We study fully BPS and a broad class of half-BPS stationary configurations of four-dimensional Euclidean N=2 supergravity with higher-derivative interactions. Working within the off-shell conformal supergravity framework of de Wit and Reys (arXiv:1706.04973), we analyse the complete set of Killing spinor equations and obtain the corresponding algebraic and differential constraints. We further derive the Euclidean attractor equations and evaluate the Wald entropy for the fully BPS AdS_2 x S^2 background. For half-BPS stationary configurations, we obtain the generalized stabilization equations expressing all fields in terms of harmonic functions on three-dimensional flat base space, extending the Lorentzian analysis of Cardoso et al (arXiv:hep-th/0009234) to the Euclidean signature. Our results provide a framework for studying supersymmetric saddles and computing the gravitational indices entirely within Euclidean higher-derivative supergravity, without recourse to analytic continuation.

hep-th.title: Modular Witten Diagrams and Quantum Extremality
hep-th.author: Abhirup Bhattacharya, Onkar Parrikar
hep-th.abstract: We study entanglement entropy for ball-shaped regions in excited states of holographic conformal field theories. The excited states are prepared by the Euclidean path integral in the CFT with a source turned on for some double-trace operator, with a small, $O(1)$ amplitude $\lambda$. On the gravity side, the double-trace operator deforms the bulk geometry as well as the entanglement structure of the state of bulk matter fields. By the quantum extremal surface formula, this leads to a deformation of the shape of the entanglement wedge, an effect which becomes manifest in the entanglement entropy at $O(\lambda^2 G_N)$. On the CFT side, we explicitly calculate the entanglement entropy perturbatively in the source amplitude to $O(\lambda^2)$, in terms of modular-flowed correlation functions of double-trace operators. We then evaluate these modular-flowed correlation functions using Witten diagrams. This calculation involves a Schwinger-Keldysh contour ordering prescription in the bulk, which we motivate using analytic continuation from Euclidean replica correlators. Focusing on a particular graviton-exchange diagram, we rewrite it in a form where it manifestly reproduces the canonical energy term present in the quantum Ryu-Takayanagi formula, including the shape deformation of the entanglement wedge due to backreaction and quantum effects.

hep-th.title: Associator Defects in Non-Unitary String-Nets
hep-th.author: Hanshi Yang
hep-th.abstract: We study obstructions to realizing fusion categories in physical Hilbert spaces by varying positive inner products on elementary fusion spaces. We introduce an associator defect to measure the smallest failure of recoupling maps to preserve the induced inner products in order to do so. By using a determinant identity from the pentagon equation, we prove that the minimum is attained and vanishes when the category is unitarizable. As an example, we compute the defect for the Yang-Lee category and its double, studying its behavior under stacking and passage to Drinfeld centers, which results in a Morita-invariant measure of bulk nonunitarity. We also obtain lower bounds for quantum-group categories with fusion multiplicities. Finally, we study how these obstructions appear in physical realizations of fusion. Under the stated assumptions on local splitting operations and coherent measurements, a positive defect imposes quantitative tradeoffs between implementation errors and operator norms. We also obtain bounds on the response to local perturbations. These results show how the failure of categorical unitarity will place quantitative constraints on physical realizations of potential fusion.

hep-th.title: Mixed-helicity bracket of celestial symmetries
hep-th.author: Daniele Pranzetti, Domenico Giuseppe Salluce
hep-th.abstract: Celestial symmetries of gravity and gauge theory can be enhanced to a $w_{1+\infty}$ algebra and an $S$-algebra respectively, when restricting to a single graviton/gluon helicity sector. Difficulties in combining both sectors in the full theory have been pointed out in the previous literature. In this work, we face this problem from the covariant phase space perspective and analyze in detail the structure of the mixed-helicity bracket of the higher-spin charges for both gravity and Yang--Mills theory. We show that, when restricting one of the two helicities to the wedge sector, a closed algebra can be obtained for all spins in terms of a notion of shadow charge we introduce. Furthermore, when focusing on the lower spin subalgebra sectors, in the case of gravity, we show that a dual mass extension of the BMS algebra can be consistently constructed; in the case of Maxwell theory, inclusion of magnetic charges allows us to recover a non-vanishing expression for the electromagnetic central charge previously obtained through different methods.

hep-th.title: Exact solution of two-dimensional Palatini Gauss-Bonnet theory on a strip
hep-th.author: Máximo Bañados, Marc Henneaux
hep-th.abstract: We analyze the two-dimensional Palatini Gauss-Bonnet theory on an infinite strip (product of a finite interval with the infinite line, corresponding to ``time"). The theory has only boundary degrees of freedom. Its phase space is the cotangent bundle to the group manifold of $SL(2,\mathbf{R})$, subject to a (first-class) constraint quadratic in the momenta. With the simplest choice of boundary Hamiltonian, namely $H = 0$, the theory is shown to describe geodesics on the group manifold of $SL(2,\mathbf{R})$, with a ``mass" determined by the Palatini Gauss-Bonnet coupling constant. Other choices of boundary Hamiltonians compatible with gauge invariance are also possible. The symmetry group contains (left and right) group translations on $SL(2,\mathbf{R})$. These are ``boundary symmetries" from the bulk point of view, one copy acting on one end of the interval, the other copy acting on the other end. Comments on the quantum theory are also given.

hep-th.title: A perturbative Liouville prescription for the celestial three-gluon amplitude
hep-th.author: Grzegorz Biskowski, Franco Ferrari, Marcin R. Piatek, Artur R. Pietrykowski
hep-th.abstract: We study the celestial three-point Mellin representation for three-gluon scattering in a dilaton background within the Mellin--Liouville formulation of Stieberger, Taylor and Zhu (STZ). We formulate an alternative perturbative prescription in which the light Liouville parameters are kept fixed in the small-$b$ expansion. Requiring global conformal covariance, a controlled light-operator expansion of the Liouville DOZZ structure constant, and consistency with the standard celestial three-gluon representation fixes the corresponding Mellin-Liouville map and operator normalization. Starting from the full Liouville three-point function, we derive the leading and first subleading terms in the $b^2$ expansion. The leading term reproduces the standard tree-level celestial Yang--Mills representation in the appropriate small-total-momentum limit, while the first subleading term is interpreted as the first coefficient of a controlled Liouville deformation of this tree-level construction. We develop an operator representation of the inverse Mellin transform, whereby polynomial dependence on the Mellin parameters is converted into differential operators acting on the leading Mellin integral. The resulting subleading contribution is obtained in closed form in terms of modified Bessel functions, with characteristic logarithmic and nonanalytic behaviour at small total momentum. Finally, we clarify the relation between the fixed-$\sigma$ and STZ finite-$b$ parametrizations by deriving the induced nonlinear reparametrization of the Mellin dimension and its action on the inverse Mellin representation. The result provides a systematic framework for studying finite-$b$ Liouville deformations and their possible relation to perturbative structures in celestial Yang-Mills theory.

hep-th.title: Probabilistic Causality from Graviton Fluctuations
hep-th.author: Giordano Cintia, Federico Piazza, Samuel Ramos
hep-th.abstract: We compute the commutator of a scalar field minimally coupled to gravity at leading order in $G_N$. The commutator is operator-valued, with terms involving derivatives of Dirac deltas supported on the Minkowski light cone. When evaluated on classical/coherent graviton states, these terms ``bend" the support of the commutator in precisely the way required to recover standard causality on a classical curved spacetime. However, these terms are also associated with a variance and are thus a source of uncertainty in the causal relations between events. We quantify this effect for a thermal state of gravitons at temperature $T$. In the large-time limit, the uncertainty of the lightcone position is given by$$ \text{Var}(\delta x) =\frac{4G_NTt}{3}\, , $$ where $\delta x$ is the displacement from the classical lightcone at $|\vec x| = t$. We obtain this result by subtracting a universal vacuum contribution that is logarithmically UV divergent and subleading at late times.

hep-th.title: Weyl conformal geometry vs Riemannian geometry of Weyl gauge invariant (dressed) metric
hep-th.author: D. M. Ghilencea, V.-M. Mandric
hep-th.abstract: Weyl conformal geometry is the natural underlying geometry of gauge theories of Weyl group (of dilatations and Poincaré symmetry), such as Weyl quadratic gravity and its generalisation, Weyl-Dirac-Born-Infeld action (WDBI). These are local, Weyl-anomaly free (quantum) gauge theories of gravity. We describe Weyl gauge symmetry from a more familiar Riemannian view of Weyl gauge invariant dressed fields by the Wilson line of dilatations. Weyl geometry can then be seen as Riemannian geometry of non-local dressed metric ($g_{\mu\nu}^*$), at the "cost" of (gauge-induced) non-commutativity in the UV, due to Wilson line. Then Weyl quadratic gravity and WDBI actions of Weyl geometry, which are Weyl gauge invariant in $d$ dimensions, have the same expression in Riemannian geometry defined by $g^*_{\mu\nu}$. This is a non-local map and dual description of the two geometries and actions in the symmetric phase. Unlike for the metric, the equation of motion of Weyl gauge field ($\omega_\mu$) does not commute with the dressing of the metric. Quantum non-locality, in particular entanglement, and non-commutativity are (gauge-invariant) physical artefacts of "translating" (local) Weyl geometry and Weyl gauge covariance into our real-world Riemannian geometry of Weyl gauge invariant observables, and they are evidence of Weyl gauge symmetry. At lower energies, $\omega_\mu$ becomes massive, can decouple and Einstein-Hilbert action and commutativity are recovered. The case of a light $\omega_\mu$ is also discussed.

hep-th.title: QFT as a set of ODEs: higher dimensions
hep-th.author: Fabiana De Cesare, Manuel Loparco
hep-th.abstract: Correlation functions of local operators in Quantum Field Theory (QFT) in Anti-de Sitter space (AdS) are completely fixed by the QFT data: the set of scaling dimensions $\Delta_i$ and OPE coefficients $C_{ijk}$ of the boundary operators, and the bulk-boundary (BOE) coefficients $b^{\hat\Phi}_i$ encoding how bulk fields decompose into boundary operators. In this work, we generalize the ordinary differential equations (ODEs) that govern the variation of the QFT data under a bulk relevant deformation, originally derived for AdS$_2$ \cite{Loparco:2026fki}, to the cases of AdS$_3$ and AdS$_4$. We demonstrate that these flow equations natively capture the mechanism of merger-annihilation when a boundary operator hits marginality, as well as level repulsion when different $\Delta_i$'s approach each other. Furthermore, we address the practical implementation of the framework: we propose substituting the ODE for the OPE coefficients with the crossing equation for greater efficiency, and we observe that Padé approximants dramatically improve the convergence of the sums over boundary operators, at least in free theories. Altogether, these advances lay the groundwork for the future application of the flow equations to the study of strongly coupled QFTs in AdS and their flat space limits.

hep-th.title: $\mathcal{N}=1$ spectra, cubic couplings and the rigid fate of DGKT
hep-th.author: Filippo Revello, Vincent Van Hemelryck
hep-th.abstract: We show that in the DGKT scenario on a generic Calabi-Yau three-fold, a recently proposed holographic constraint on cubic couplings is satisfied if and only if the Calabi-Yau is rigid, i.e. when $h^{2,1}=0$. More generally, we illustrate how in 4d $\mathcal{N}=1$ supergravity, extremal cubic couplings are determined by the third derivatives of the real, Kähler-invariant superpotential, while the eigenvalues of its Hessian compute the conformal dimensions of the dual scalar operators. These results extend more broadly beyond 4d $\mathcal{N}=1$ supergravity. Applying them to supersymmetric DGKT vacua, we prove that extremal cubic couplings always vanish in the Kähler + universal CS/dilaton sector, whereas non-vanishing (super-)extremal couplings are always present in the complex structure sector. It follows that the holographic constraint is satisfied in DGKT if and only if the Calabi-Yau three-fold is rigid with $h^{2,1}=0$.

hep-th.title: A Novel Matrix Model for the M5-brane?
hep-th.author: Manuel Artime, Ralph Blumenhagen, Thomas Raml
hep-th.abstract: We provide a new formal extension of the BFSS matrix model by an additional 5-bracket. Maximal supersymmetry leads us to promote the BFSS 2-bracket structure constants to a dynamical field $H_{abc}$ governed by a Chern-Simons-like kinetic term. We first show that the full generic pseudo-action is invariant under maximal supersymmetry and that the associated supersymmetry algebra closes upon invoking a number of BPS-like quadratic constraints. We then present a special case based on the 5-Lie algebra $A_6$ that evades these additional constraints and allows for a Lagrangian description. These results hinge on a conspiracy of properties of the $SO(9)$ gamma matrices and the 2- and 5-brackets. Compellingly, the resulting model seems to realize some features expected of a theory containing M5-branes and opens up the possibility of further including higher brackets for the M6- and M9-branes.

hep-th.title: Gravitational Memory Beyond Null Infinity through Finite-Distance Carrollian Screens
hep-th.author: Felipe Diaz, Sercan Hüsnügil, Oriana Labrin, Leonardo Sanhueza
hep-th.abstract: We investigate gravitational memory beyond null infinity by studying finite-distance null hypersurfaces endowed with Carrollian geometry. We show that the intrinsic degenerate geometry, optical data, and null Brown--York tensor of a finite null screen define a quasilocal Carrollian dissipative system, providing a natural framework to characterize the residual geometric response after the passage of radiation. To make this construction explicit and compare it with the standard asymptotic description, we use Robinson--Trautman spacetimes as an exactly solvable radiative setting. For asymptotically flat Robinson--Trautman geometries, we transform the solution to Bondi gauge and extract the asymptotic data directly in terms of the Robinson--Trautman field. In the linearized sector, the Bondi shear is purely electric and produces the standard displacement-memory effect associated with the relaxation toward the final Schwarzschild geometry. We show that the leading large-radius tracefree component of the finite-screen memory reduces to the Bondi displacement memory, while finite-distance corrections retain additional focusing, embedding dependence, angular drift, Coulombic data, and near-zone information. Thus, Bondi memory emerges as the universal asymptotic projection of a broader quasilocal Carrollian response. Late-time screens approaching the final Schwarzschild horizon exhibit exponentially decaying non-isotropic Carrollian data, leaving only the isotropic null Brown--York stress. As a by-product, we construct the Robinson--Trautman solution with nonzero cosmological constant to second order in the radiative amplitude and use the holographic dictionary to study the associated energy fluxes and find that the resulting charge does not obey a universal monotonicity property.

hep-th.title: Primordial Correlators from a Kaluza-Klein Graviton Continuum
hep-th.author: Shuntaro Aoki
hep-th.abstract: Cosmological collider signals are usually discussed for isolated massive particles, whose exchange produces characteristic logarithmic oscillations in primordial correlators. In this work, we study how this signal is modified when the exchanged states form a continuous mass spectrum. We first develop a spectral representation for inflationary correlators mediated by a continuum field. In the soft limit, the non-analytic part of the seed function is expressed as a Fourier--Laplace transform of the spectral weight with respect to logarithmic momentum variables. This representation shows that a continuum superposes clock signals with different frequencies and can dephase the sharp oscillation associated with a single massive particle. We then realize this mechanism in an RS2-like inflationary braneworld, where the inflaton is localized on a de Sitter brane in a five-dimensional AdS bulk. The tensor sector contains a localized massless graviton and a continuum of Kaluza-Klein gravitons starting at \(m=3H/2\). We derive the KK wavefunctions and identify the brane spectral weight fixed by the continuum wavefunction on the brane. Applying this weight to the inflaton four-point function, we find a smooth seed function rather than a persistent logarithmic clock oscillation. This behavior follows from the fact that the continuum starts at zero clock frequency, while the KK spectral weight vanishes near threshold. Our results provide a concrete higher-dimensional example in which deviations from the standard cosmological collider signal encode the structure of a continuum high-energy spectrum.

hep-th.title: Stokes Phenomena between AdS/CFT and dS/CFT
hep-th.author: Masazumi Honda, Kotaro Shinmyo
hep-th.abstract: As parameters are varied, the set of saddle points contributing to a (path) integral may change discontinuously, leading to a corresponding change in the asymptotic expansion of the integral. This behavior is known as the Stokes phenomenon. We explore this phenomenon in the context of the analytic continuation problem relating the AdS/CFT and dS/CFT correspondences. In this paper, we study these correspondences for three-dimensional pure gravity and two-dimensional Liouville theory, using independent calculations in bulk minisuperspace and in the boundary Liouville zero-mode. In the bulk, the dS contour selects a single saddle and yields the tunneling wave function. Upon continuation to AdS, the contour instead selects an infinite family of saddles. The boundary calculation independently reproduces the same Stokes structure at leading semiclassical order, providing a nontrivial holographic consistency check. Our construction also offers a contour prescription for the conformal factor problem in Euclidean AdS$_3$ quantum gravity within minisuperspace.

hep-th.title: Monopoles, duality, and energy splitting in Chern-Simons QED$_3$
hep-th.author: Shai M. Chester, Éric Dupuis
hep-th.abstract: We compute the scaling dimensions of monopole operators in QED$_3$ with $N$ 2-component complex fermions and Chern-Simons level $k$ to subleading order in the limit where $k,N$ are large and $k/N$ is fixed, which generalizes previous results for scalar QED$_3$ (sQED$_3$) coupled to $N$ complex scalars. In both cases, at leading large $N$ many monopole operators are degenerate, and we compute their energy splitting. We use these results to check the duality between QED$_3$ with $N=1,k=-3/2$ and sQED$_3$ with $N=1,k=2$, whose $U(1)$ monopole symmetry is enhanced to $SO(3)$. We find the scaling dimensions in each dual theory match to high precision for all charges, the lowest charge spin 1 monopoles are close to 2 as expected for the emergent $SO(3)$ current, and the degenerate second lowest charge monopoles match a prediction from a fuzzy sphere calculation, including the energy splitting. We also find similar evidence for dualities between QED$_3$ with $N=1,k=-(2m+1)/2$ and one scalar coupled to two $U(1)$ gauge fields, which has an effective description as sQED$_3$ with $N=1,k=\frac{m+1}{m}$ and $q_s=mq_f$ for $m>1$. Finally, we also find similar evidence for Son's duality between QED$_3$ with $N=1,k=0$ and a free fermion, and clarify a previously discussed match between sQED$_3$ with $N=k=1$ dual to a free fermion.

hep-th.title: Spontaneous symmetry breaking as a mechanism for the Gribov scale in a BRST-invariant formulation
hep-th.author: M.A.L.Capri, V. E. R. Lemes
hep-th.abstract: We propose a BRST-invariant formulation of the Gribov--Zwanziger model in the Landau gauge, in which the Gribov scale is produced by the spontaneous breaking of a scalar quartet symmetry, rather than through the explicit breaking term of the conventional construction. We show that the resulting action preserves the ghost equation of the Landau gauge and reproduces the characteristic Gribov-type gauge propagator of the original Gribov scenario, a BRST-invariant mass term of the refined type being accommodated by the same mechanism. We establish the renormalizability of the model to all orders by means of algebraic renormalization techniques, no counterterm being required outside those already present in the classical action. We further show that the condensation of the quartet leaves unchanged the cohomology through which the observables are characterized, the operator realized in the displaced vacuum having the same cohomology as that of the symmetric phase, so that the mass scale is produced at no cost in the physical content of the theory, and the construction of genuine gauge-invariant observables in the Gribov--Zwanziger setting is thereby left open to the usual cohomological methods.

hep-th.title: Extremal black hole mimickers: geometry, stability, and long-delay signal trains
hep-th.author: Sergey N. Solodukhin
hep-th.abstract: We present a spacetime that serves as a horizonless mimicker of extremal black holes. Unlike previously studied mimickers of black holes with non-degenerate horizons, whose geometries are of the wormhole type and consist of two asymptotically flat regions connected by a very long throat, the mimicker of an extremal black hole possesses a single asymptotically flat region at one end and an infinitely long throat at the other. In the throat region, the spacetime approaches the direct-product geometry $M_{1,1} \times S^2$, where $M_{1,1}$ is two-dimensional Minkowski spacetime and $S^2$ is the two-sphere. We investigate scalar-field dynamics and the fate of the Aretakis instability. Although Aretakis-like modes arise in a local analysis of the throat, they do not lead to a physical instability of the mimicker. A scalar perturbation initially localized in the throat gives rise, at late times, to a sequence of signals with a characteristic separation $t_{\rm delay}\sim 1/\lambda$, where $\lambda\ll 1$ is a deformation parameter. This timescale is parametrically larger than the echo time $t_{\rm echo}\sim \ln(1/\lambda)$ characteristic of non-extremal black-hole mimickers. We refer to this sequence as a {\it long-delay signal train}. Geometrically, the periodicity of the long-delay signals is associated with periodic geodesics on $S^2$. We then extend the construction to extremal Kerr. In this case, the throat region approaches a generalized product geometry involving $M_{1,1}$ and a two-dimensional surface $\Sigma_2$. The corresponding signals are expected to form a quasi-periodic signal train, reflecting the quasi-periodic geodesic motion on $\Sigma_2$. We also comment on the generalization to wormhole mimickers of non-extremal black holes and on the implications of these results for unitarity in the context of the AdS/CFT correspondence.

hep-th.title: Nambu's Dynamics, Strings and Gravitized Quantum Theory
hep-th.author: Tristan Hübsch, Djordje Minic
hep-th.abstract: In this article we present a new view on string theory that is rooted in quantum foundations extended to the domain of quantum gravity in the form of gravitized quantum theory, in which the canonical probability measure captured by the Born rule of quantum theory, turns out to be dynamical and contextual. We claim that this gravitization of quantum theory is the essence of string theory. String theory, according to this view, originates in foundations of quantum theory and Nambu's dynamics, which features in the non-perturbative definition of string theory in terms of a T-duality covariant and non-commutative formulation, called the metastring. Nambu's dynamics and the associated cubic and hypercubic objects also appear as the natural language for exploring the new observables and phenomena implied by a dynamical Born rule, including triple and higher order quantum interference, that can be investigated in experiments involving massive quantum probes, and that are also needed for direct empirical tests of the Born rule, a cornerstone of quantum theory.

hep-th.title: Near-horizon BF bounds for the $t^+$ KK tower on extremal AdS$_5$ black holes
hep-th.author: Xiao-Long Liu, Zheng Miao, Yuezhang Tang
hep-th.abstract: We study the charged Breitenlohner--Freedman (BF) bound for all horizon harmonics of the type IIB $t^+$ Kaluza--Klein tower on extremal charged AdS$_5$ black holes with equal rotations. The scalar equation follows from maximal five-dimensional gauged supergravity at level zero and the linearized exceptional-field-theory equations at higher levels. For aligned charge and rotation, a quadratic form in charge and spin changes signature on the curve of supersymmetric (BPS) black holes, where every mode satisfies the bound. Above the curve, where $\Omega_H>1$, every black hole has a violating mode, although no finite truncation in level or spin detects violation at every such black hole. Below the curve, where $\Phi_H>1$, the BF-passing set is confined to a thin strip and controlled by charge and spin discreteness. At large radius and fixed rotation, a level-four mode with spin proportional to the radius violates the bound even where all U(2) singlets satisfy it. These results concern the near-horizon BF bound of one tower in two-derivative supergravity; full radial stability remains open.

hep-th.title: Regge bounds and eikonal estimates in scalar effective field theory
hep-th.author: Ji Li
hep-th.abstract: Positivity bounds are derived from twice-subtracted dispersion relations, which hold only if the amplitude grows more slowly than $s^2$. For the massless shift-symmetric scalar with $g_4(\partial\phi)^4/\Lambda^4$ and $g_6(\partial\phi)^6/\Lambda^8$, we derive the dispersion relation, whose cuts start at zero energy, and study the large-$s$ growth at fixed $t<0$ of the tree, the one-loop bubble and the three-loop banana. The partial-wave sum is split at a transition spin: low spins are bounded by unitarity, channel by channel, and high spins are evaluated with the eikonal phase of the crossed-channel logarithms by stationary phase. Matching the two regions gives the phase-model growth $s^{8/7}$ for the quartic sector and $s^{16/15}$ for the sextic sector, while a transition scale fixed by the cutoff gives the conditional bound $s^{7/4}$; in the forward limit the same construction gives only the marginal growth $s^2$, so that Regge boundedness remains an assumption on the completion. Under this assumption the $2\to 2$ and $2\to 4$ absorptive parts below the cutoff restrict the couplings to $0<g_4\le 80\pi^2/7$ and $-7.2\times 10^5\lesssim g_6\lesssim 6.9\times 10^5$.

hep-th.title: Pohlmeyer reduction of Newton-Cartan strings
hep-th.author: Aritra Banerjee
hep-th.abstract: We develop a Pohlmeyer-type reduction for classical non-relativistic strings on string Newton-Cartan backgrounds. For strings on a two-sphere, we identify the invariant reduced field, show that its dynamics is integrable, and construct a Lax representation. We relate this intrinsic formulation to the non-relativistic expansion of relativistic strings and obtain a dictionary between non-relativistic string solutions and their reduced counterparts. The construction explicitly determines which relativistic solitonic configurations survive the non-relativistic limit and which decouple. Moreover, it provides a framework for applying integrability methods to Newton-Cartan string dynamics.

hep-th.title: Spectral function, OPE, and QNMs detect different singular points of black branes with unequal R-charges
hep-th.author: Hyunwoo Oh
hep-th.abstract: We consider black brane solutions in the STU model, with three R-charges labeled by the parameters $q_1,q_2,q_3$. For equal R-charges $q_1=q_2=q_3$, the solution becomes the Reissner-Nordström black brane. For unequal R-charges $q_1>q_2>q_3\geq0$, there are three curvature singular points at $R\equiv r^2=-q_i$. Only $R=-q_3$ is the physical singularity, and the other two lie beyond it. Their optical times $T_i$, the complex times of null rays from the boundary to these singular points and back, form a right triangle in the complex $T$-plane. We probe these singular points using three observables, all built from the retarded correlator of $T_{xy}$ at zero spatial momentum: spectral function, OPE coefficients, and QNMs. The exponentially small correction to the spectral function at large real frequency is dominated by $T_1$ and $T_2$, which have the smallest ${\rm Im}\,T_i$. The OPE convergence radius is determined by $T_1$, which has the smallest $|T_i|$. A line of QNMs lies along the direction of $1/T_2$, since $T_2$ has the smallest phase $\arg T_i$. Furthermore, there is a second line of QNMs along the negative imaginary axis, which carries information about $T_3$ corresponding to the physical singularity. We derive these results from a WKB analysis and check them numerically. The three observables are therefore sensitive to different singular points of the geometry.

hep-th.title: Landau-Ginzburg Theory of a Holographic Superconductor: A Horizon Perspective on the Zero-Temperature Ground State
hep-th.author: Sejin Kim, Yunseok Seo
hep-th.abstract: We investigate the effect of a quartic scalar self-interaction, $\lambda|\phi|^4$, on a holographic superconductor in which non-linear electrodynamic couplings generate a superconducting dome containing an extended Lifshitz regime. The quartic interaction leaves the linearized scalar dynamics around the normal phase unchanged while modifying the non-linear solutions where the scalar field is large. As $\lambda$ increases, the solutions within the dome pass through three stages. The Lifshitz region shrinks until its scaling solution disappears at $\lambda^*$, leaving a no-AdS region, beyond whose edge the flows end before reaching any asymptotic region, and above $\lambda_c$ the dome consists entirely of asymptotically AdS hairy black holes. At the bottom of the dome we identify the point where the horizon value of the scalar field is largest, which we refer to as the critical point. There this value lies at the deepest symmetry-breaking minimum that the horizon effective potential, of Landau-Ginzburg form, can have. Unlike a conventional Landau-Ginzburg description, this interpretation rests on the scalar field at the horizon rather than on the boundary order parameter. Below $\lambda^*$, the constant scalar of the Lifshitz fixed point sits instead at the minimum of the effective potential of its asymptotic scaling region.

hep-th.title: Landau Theory of Black Brane Phase Transitions from Kasner Singularities
hep-th.author: Hong-Da Lyu
hep-th.abstract: We develop a Landau theory of a continuous black-brane phase transition using the geometry of the black-hole interior. The normal phase has a Reissner--Nordström Cauchy horizon, whereas the scalarized phase ends at a Kasner singularity. A conserved radial charge determines the grand potential from either endpoint and permits a direct phase comparison. At the critical point, we show analytically that the quadratic correction to the conserved radial charge vanishes. Using the inverse Kasner scalar velocity as an interior order parameter, we then construct a Landau potential whose coefficients are determined entirely from the terminal singularity. The Iyer--Wald first law relates this potential to the conventional boundary Landau theory and fixes its quartic coefficient. For two models with different scalar self-interactions, the resulting theory predicts the critical scaling of the Kasner order parameter and the grand-potential difference between the phases, in agreement with fully backreacted numerical solutions.

hep-th.title: Covariant Wigner--Weyl calculus, non-dissipative transport and the chiral anomaly in inhomogeneous systems with nontrivial momentum-space topology
hep-th.author: M.A.Zubkov
hep-th.abstract: We review, systematize and extend the covariant Wigner--Weyl calculus for fermions in non-Abelian gauge fields and its applications to systems inhomogeneous in coordinate space with nontrivial momentum-space topology: the non-Abelian chiral separation and quantum Hall effects, their stability under interactions, the Fermi-surface invariant of inhomogeneous systems and the non-elliptic models that carry it, the factorization of the chiral anomaly into the instanton number and the momentum-space invariant $N_3$, and the noncommutative-geometric form of the invariants.

hep-th.title: Equivariant Localization with Electric Monodromy in M-theory
hep-th.author: Ji-seong Chae
hep-th.abstract: We extend equivariant localization for supersymmetric AdS$_3$ backgrounds of M-theory to solutions with nonzero electric flux periods. The associated local electric potential acquires additive monodromy, contributing to the warped volume alongside R-symmetry fixed points and outer boundaries. Using Killing-spinor identities, we relate the electric periods to magnetic flux and, for a class of compact backgrounds, the warped volume to the electric Maxwell charge. We also derive a relation between the gravitational anomaly and the electric flux. We apply these results to AdS$_3$ $\times S^3 \times S^3 \times T^2$ and AdS$_3$ $\times S^3 \times K3 \times S^1$, recovering their central charges and deriving the R-current levels of the former directly from eleven-dimensional supergravity. Finally, we study a noncompact half-BPS AdS$_3$ $\times S^3\times S^3$ geometry fibered over a periodic half-cylinder, where fixed-point, monodromy and outer-boundary contributions coexist.

hep-th.title: Vacuum correlations of the stress-energy-momentum tensor with constituent quarks
hep-th.author: Mirko Serino, Wojciech Broniowski, Enrique Ruiz Arriola
hep-th.abstract: The two point correlation function of the stress-energy-momentum tensor describes the propagation of a space-time ``micro-earthquake'' in the vacuum. In the framework of the path integral formulation of field theory in curved space-time, we discuss the Ward-Takashi identity for two-point Green's function of the stress-energy-momentum tensor for a general case of a non-conformal theory. The identity constrains the longitudinal part of the correlator, with the vacuum expectation value of the stress-energy-momentum, non-zero in a non-conformal theory. The obtained formula is demonstrated on the free massive Dirac fermion theory, treated at the one-loop level. This example befits a class of phenomenological chiral quarks models which have been used successfully in numerous applications in the soft non-perturbative regime of strong interactions. We stress the role of the constraints following from the Ward-Takahashi identity for the correlation functions in these models and point out the differences with the low-energy theorems (sum rules), not complying to the symmetry requirements. We also show the temporal representation of the two-point correlators, which is an object amenable to lattice QCD simulations.

hep-th.title: Relativistic Navier-Stokes description of the quark-gluon plasma radial flow
hep-th.author: Yago Bea
hep-th.abstract: Using relativistic Navier-Stokes in the well-posed Bemfica-Disconzi-Noronha-Kovtun (BDNK) formulation, with a QCD equation of state and transport coefficients, we perform simulations that describe the radial flow in central Pb-Pb collisions measured at the LHC, providing a proof of principle for its viability in heavy-ion phenomenology. We identify causal frames that retain the Landau-frame interpretation, and verify frame robustness. Müller-Israel-Stewart simulations with identical input show large second-order effects, exceeding the frame dependence of relativistic Navier-Stokes, as well as causality violations.

hep-th.title: Quantum-information bounds on black-hole evaporation and de Sitter expansion
hep-th.author: Rong-Gen Cai, Li Hu, Shao-Jiang Wang
hep-th.abstract: It is well-known that the unitary nature of black hole evaporation enforces its entropy evolution to follow the Page curve. In this Letter, we further explore the outcome of the quantum speed limit on how fast a quantum system can evolve unitarily. When combined with the maximal information transmission bound, we place upper limits on the evaporation rates of dynamical black-hole entropy and mass that are otherwise divergent at the very end of the Hawking evaporation, during which the Penrose inequality from the cosmic censorship conjecture is consistently obeyed. Further applying the maximal information transmission bound to an effective-field-theory description for all sub-horizon regions of a de Sitter space would sufficiently reproduce a weaker trans-Planckian censorship conjecture up to a numeric prefactor conditionally.

hep-th.title: Precision Measurements of the Electroweak Mixing Angle in the Region of the Z pole at the Large Hadron Collider
hep-th.author: Arie Bodek, Hyon-San Seo, Un-Ki Yang
hep-th.abstract: In the Standard Model (SM), the effective leptonic weak mixing angle $\sin^2\theta^\ell_{\rm eff}$ can be predicted to very high accuracy by using the experimental values of the mass of the Z boson ($M_Z$), the Fermi constant, the fine structure constant, the mass of Higgs boson, the quark masses, and the value of the Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) strong coupling ($\alpha_s$) at $M_Z$. Therefore, deviations of measurements from SM predictions can be indications of new physics. With recent advances in experimental and analysis techniques, measurements of $\sin^2\theta^\ell_{\rm eff}$ at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), extracted from the forward-backward asymmetry ($A_{\rm FB}$) in Drell-Yan dilepton events, are now competitive with previously published measurements at $e^+e^-$ collider experiments. We report on a more precise extraction of the effective leptonic weak mixing angle via an updated analysis of the CMS Drell-Yan $A_{\rm FB}$ measurements at 13 TeV. We obtain $\sin^2\theta^\ell_{\rm eff}$=0.23154$\pm$0.00024 with additional PDF constraints from measurements of the W decay lepton charge asymmetry at 13 TeV and the W/Z cross section ratios. It is the most precise single experiment measurement to date and is in excellent agreement with the SM 2026 indirect prediction of 0.23152$\pm$0.00006.

hep-th.title: Chiral gapped states are universally non-topological
hep-th.author: Xiang Li, Ting-Chun Lin, Yahya Alavirad, John McGreevy
hep-th.abstract: We propose an operator generalization of the Li-Haldane conjecture regarding the entanglement Hamiltonian of a disk in a 2+1D chiral gapped groundstate. The logic applies to regions with sharp corners, from which we derive several universal properties regarding corner entanglement. These universal properties follow from a set of locally-checkable conditions on the wavefunction. We also define a quantity $(\mathfrak{c}_{\text{tot}})_{\text{min}}$ that reflects the robustness of corner entanglement contributions, and show that it provides an obstruction to a gapped boundary. One reward from our analysis is that we can construct a local gapped Hamiltonian within the same chiral gapped phase from a given wavefunction; we conjecture that it is closer to the low-energy renormalization group fixed point than the original parent Hamiltonian. Our analysis of corner entanglement reveals the emergence of a universal conformal geometry encoded in the entanglement structure of bulk regions of chiral gapped states that is not visible in topological field theory. Our formalism also gives an explanation of the modular commutator formula for the chiral central charge.

hep-th.title: Bulk viscosity of a binary mixture: the role of the intra-species interaction
hep-th.author: Gabriele Parisi, Vincenzo Nugara, Shams Ul Arfeen, Salvatore Plumari, Vincenzo Greco
hep-th.abstract: The bulk viscosity $\zeta$ is a transport coefficient which is of central importance for various areas of modern physics. In particular, its determination for a fluid with two components is challenging, since it involves a complex interplay of multiple microscopic processes that operate on different time scales. Within the Chapman-Enskog framework, based on a series expansion of the Boltzmann distribution function, many previous works have derived the 1$^{\text{st}}$ order result for the $\zeta$ of a mixture. However, such a result fails to reproduce relevant physical features of the system, especially when the masses of the two components are similar. In this work we improve the 1$^{\text{st}}$ order Chapman-Enskog result by deriving the $\zeta$ at the 2$^{\text{nd}}$ order in the expansion. We show that this improved formula encodes many physical properties that the 1$^{\text{st}}$ order result misses: under specific conditions, the 2$^{\text{nd}}$ order result can be qualitatively and quantitatively very different from the 1$^{\text{st}}$ order one. Moreover, this result is compared against the $\zeta$ evaluated within the Green-Kubo formalism, by means of a numerical solution of the Relativistic Boltzmann equation. The agreement with respect to this benchmark is significantly improved when moving from the 1$^{\text{st}}$ to the 2$^{\text{nd}}$ order CE result.

hep-th.title: A friendly phantom: Late-time AdS-to-dS transition and cosmological tensions
hep-th.author: Özgür Akarsu, Leandros Perivolaropoulos, A. Emrah Yükselci, Alexander Zhuk
hep-th.abstract: We present Ph-$\Lambda_{\rm s}$CDM, a phantom-scalar realization within general relativity of the sign-switching cosmological-constant idea, $\Lambda_{\rm s}$CDM, in which a phantom scalar evolving on a bounded hyperbolic-tangent potential induces a smooth mirror AdS-to-dS transition in the late-time dark-energy density. The wrong-sign kinetic term, usually viewed as pathological, becomes the mechanism lifting the field from a negative- to a positive-energy vacuum-like regime. The construction also shows that the field can become repulsive while its energy density is still negative. The cosmology nevertheless remains controlled: total energy stays positive, the late-time attractor is de Sitter rather than a Big Rip, and the dynamics remain safely infrared. Ph-$\Lambda_{\rm s}$CDM thus offers a concrete late-time mechanism with the potential to address multiple cosmological tensions.

hep-th.title: First look at the evaluation of two-loop Feynman integrals for radiative return processes
hep-th.author: Mattia Pozzoli, William J. Torres Bobadilla
hep-th.abstract: Precision studies of radiative return processes at low-energy electron--positron colliders require next-to-next-to-leading order QED predictions retaining full dependence on the electron mass. We present the calculation of planar two-loop four-point Feynman integrals relevant for initial-state radiation contributions to these processes. The calculation presents considerable analytical complexity, due to the presence of a nested square root and of integrals associated with elliptic geometries. We construct differential equations for the Feynman integrals which are polynomial in the dimensional regulator, and are suitable for numerical integration. We demonstrate stable numerical evaluations throughout the physical region relevant for low-energy experiments, despite the presence of large hierarchies of scales. Our results provide essential building blocks for NNLO predictions for radiative return processes.

hep-th.title: Left-right symmetry breaking in $E_6^L\times E_6^R$ occurs only in spacetime -- with possible implications for strong $CP$
hep-th.author: Tejinder P. Singh
hep-th.abstract: Two-sided octonionic $E_6^L\times E_6^R$ unification trinifies each factor and so carries two colour groups: the visible $SU(3)_c$ and a second $SU(3)_{c'}$ which, gauged like the first, would colour the charged lepton and must be suppressed by hand. We argue no such device is needed: the left-right symmetry acts in spacetime, not internally -- in the gravi-weak reading $SU(2)_R$ is the gravitational frame group and the exchange is ordinary parity on the Dirac field; a spacetime operation cannot double the internal colour. Colour is single and vector-like, $SU(3)_{c'}=SU(3)_c$, and the electron is a colour singlet. The right sector contributes one colour-blind datum, $\sqrt m$ (values: the exceptional-Jordan trace split, an input; $N_R$ fixes only the colour representation). An anomaly no-go shows that no gauged $U(1)$ on the visible fermions can carry the $\sqrt m$ pattern: the dark-electromagnetic $U(1)_{\rm dem}$ carries the parity mirror of electric charge on the dark sector, the visible fermions are dem-neutral, and no visible fifth force is predicted. Hypercharge is recovered as the consistency relation $Y=Q-T^3_L$, $Q=N/3$. As an application, parity restricts the QCD angle to $\{0,\pi\}$; $\theta_{\rm QCD}=0$ is selected, not derived, by matching to the sign content of the quark mass determinant, whose phase vanishes because the flavour rotors have real determinant. Hence $\bar\theta=0$ at tree level, conditional on the gravi-weak identification, with a nonzero CKM phase. Loop stability is open: the two-loop $\bar\theta$ of the minimal universal-seesaw parity model arises from scalar exchange, so the absence of a gauged $W_R$ here does not remove its mechanism, which the Higgs-bridge sector shares. We tag throughout what is derived, what is input, and what is open.

hep-th.title: Nonlinear particle detectors across the Rindler firewall
hep-th.author: Matheus H. Zambianco, Eduardo Martín-Martínez
hep-th.abstract: We investigate Unruh-DeWitt detectors coupled to composite observables of a quantum scalar field, including quadratic coupling to the field momentum and coupling to the local energy density. We develop a distributional framework for evaluating the corresponding detector response functions and apply it to detectors crossing the Rindler firewall. While we recover the finite response of the derivative-coupling model, we show that quadratic momentum coupling leads to products of distributions that do not admit a canonical, regulator-independent definition in the sharp-firewall idealization. The vacuum correspondence between the local energy-density and quadratic momentum responses motivates the conjecture that analogous difficulties may arise for energy-density coupling in the sharp firewall model. Within the sharp, pointlike composite-coupling model considered here, our analysis further suggests that these pathologies originate from the discontinuous severing of correlations across the Rindler horizon.

hep-th.title: Inflation in unimodular loop quantum cosmology
hep-th.author: Steffen Gielen, Rita B. Neves
hep-th.abstract: We study inflation in the setting of unimodular loop quantum cosmology, where time evolution is defined in unimodular time rather than with respect to a free, massless scalar field as is standard in loop quantum cosmology. The unimodular setting leads to a natural Schrödinger time evolution in a time coordinate with clear geometric meaning, defined independently of any particular matter content; an inflaton can be included but is not needed as a clock. We review the unimodular version of loop quantum cosmology and comment on possible connections to full (unimodular) loop quantum gravity. Then, focusing on semiclassical effective equations, we derive analytical solutions in simple cases such as a constant potential, emphasising the use of a unimodular time coordinate. We also discuss numerical solutions for phenomenologically interesting cases such as a quadratic potential and Starobinsky inflation, comparing different possible choices of initial conditions. In particular, we show that choosing an $\alpha$-attractor potential allows for models of a bounce either dominated by kinetic or potential energy, which are compatible with observations while potentially including observable imprints of the quantum-gravity regime.

hep-th.title: GOOFy-compatible 3HDMs and beyond
hep-th.author: I. de Medeiros Varzielas, A. Kunčinas
hep-th.abstract: Beyond conventional Higgs-family and general CP transformations, one may also consider a broader class of non-standard "GOOFy" transformations, in which the scalar fields and their conjugates are assigned related but inequivalent transformations. Although these transformations are not symmetries of a full Lagrangian in the conventional sense, some nevertheless stabilise the scalar potential. Their impact on the quadratic sector has not yet been systematically classified. We develop a sign-orbit technique to determine the bilinear structures compatible with these transformations. Applied to three-Higgs-doublet models, and formulated so as to extend to larger multi-Higgs sectors, the method shows that a non-vanishing GOOFy-compatible quadratic sector exists only when two independent conditions are met: the underlying group admits a non-trivial sign character, and that character is realised within the tensor product of the scalar representation and its conjugate. As a key consequence, we demonstrate that the renormalisation-group stability of the $r_0 \to -r_0$ manifold in isolation is not a generic feature of multi-Higgs potentials, but rather a direct consequence of special algebraic properties of $SU(2)$. These results provide a classification of the admissible GOOFy quadratic structures and their invariant bilinear subspaces, highlighting the algebraic obstructions to their renormalisation-group stability.

hep-th.title: Quadratic effective energy--momentum tensor on uniform-density hypersurfaces during slow-roll inflation
hep-th.author: Inyong Cho
hep-th.abstract: We investigate the quadratic-order effective energy-momentum tensor (2EMT) of scalar cosmological perturbations on uniform-density hypersurfaces during slow-roll inflation. The 2EMT is a gauge-fixed effective source rather than a gauge-invariant observable. We impose the complete scalar gauge conditions $\delta\rho=0$ and $E=0$, express all perturbations in terms of the Bardeen potential $\Psi$, and distinguish the strict infrared and ultraviolet limits from the intermediate regimes. The uniform-density time shift differs from the comoving one by an explicitly gradient-suppressed term, $Q_{\mathrm{UD}}-Q_{\mathrm{C}}=-\Delta\Psi/[3{\mathcal H}({\mathcal H}'-{\mathcal H}^2)]$. The two sources vanish at zero gradient, while their first nonzero infrared coefficients differ and give $w_{\rm raw}\simeq-1/3$ at leading slow-roll order. In the intermediate infrared, all four gauges have this leading ratio, with gauge-dependent amplitudes. In the ultraviolet, the longitudinal, spatially-flat, and comoving gauges give $w_{\rm raw}\simeq1/3$, whereas the uniform-density gauge gives $w_{\rm raw}\simeq1$. The common $1/\epsilon$ enhancement of the matter-clock gauges reflects the slow evolution of their clocks; the additional uniform-density $1/\sigma_2^2$ enhancement originates from the Laplacian contribution to the density constraint. Neither enhancement is interpreted as a gauge-independent physical instability, and the gauge reconstruction must remain perturbatively small.

hep-th.title: Gravitational waves flooding the Universe after wall domination
hep-th.author: Sabir Ramazanov, Zhen-Min Zeng
hep-th.abstract: We discuss a possible early Universe scenario, where radiation era is interrupted by the epoch of domination of domain walls eventually annihilating into particles. During this period the Universe undergoes accelerated expansion, while the comoving correlation length of the domain wall network remains constant. The network serves as a source of tensor modes, which get frozen upon exiting the horizon similarly to the case of inflationary fluctuations. The modes re-enter the horizon during the subsequent stage of radiation domination and since then contribute to the gravitational wave background. The period of wall domination is manifested in the spectral shape of gravitational waves via a distinctive plateau replacing a peak, which is characteristic for the scenario with sub-dominant walls. The gravitational waves are strong enough to be observed with present-day and future facilities in a broad range of frequencies. In particular, their energy density is sufficient to produce a significant impact on the effective number of neutrino species, unless the duration of wall domination is suitably constrained.

hep-th.title: An Orbital Curvature for ISCOs
hep-th.author: Poulami Mukherjee, Chandrasekhar Bhamidipati, Sudipta Mukherji
hep-th.abstract: Building on the fact that circular orbits are the fixed points of the phase portraits arising from the geodesic equations on a black hole spacetime, we develop a general orbital geometry, which captures the stability structure of orbits. The construction uses the orbital energy, angular momentum and angular velocity as state space variables, with response functions encoding how the circular orbits react to changes in the black hole background and in their angular motion. The associated scalar curvature provides a geometric diagnostic of certain distinguished points of the circular orbit family, such as the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO), where it becomes singular. Across the ISCO, the relevant orbital response functions change sign as the system passes from the stable to the unstable circular orbit branch, and are found to vanish at marginal stability. We illustrate the framework for Schwarzschild black holes in asymptotically flat four dimensions, and five dimensional Schwarzschild AdS spacetimes. In the four dimensional case, the ISCO is associated with a degeneration of the energy response sector, while in the five dimensional AdS case it is detected through the angular response. The AdS example also exhibits a separate curvature singularity at a point which coincides with the minimum temperature of the black hole background. These results show that the orbital geometry provides a promising unified framework for characterizing the stability of circular orbits and criticality of ISCOs.

hep-th.title: Integrals of motion for the deformed $W$-algebra $W_{q,t}(D_l)$
hep-th.author: Michio Jimbo, Takeo Kojima
hep-th.abstract: The deformed $W$-algebra $W_{q,t}(D_l)$ of type $D_l$ possesses an infinite family of commuting elements that can be viewed as a two-parameter deformation of the classical Hamiltonians for the KdV hierarchy of type $D_l$; these conserved charges are termed local integrals of motion (IMs). Concurrently, the quantum toroidal algebra $U_q(D_l^{"})$ of type $D_l$ admits four distinct representations via free field realizations, each corresponding to one of the four end nodes of the affine Dynkin diagram. Utilizing these representations, we associate an infinite set of commuting operators with each node, which we define as non-local integrals of motion. Both local and non-local integrals of motion act simultaneously on a shared Fock space consisting of $l+1$ free fields. We provide a direct, computational proof demonstrating that these local and non-local integrals of motion mutually commute.
